## 9.25.2 Steel Renewal (2024)

Steel renewal is required where the gauged thickness is less than $t _ { n e t } + 0 . 5$ mm $( \mathrm { \Delta } t _ { n e t } + 0 . 0 2 \ \mathrm { \Delta i n . } )$ for

Single skin hatch covers,

The plating of double skin hatch covers, and

● Coaming structures the corrosion additions $t _ { S }$ of which are provided in [TABLE 8] .

Where the gauged thickness is within the $\begin{array} { r l } { \mathrm { r a n g e } ~ } & { { } t _ { n e t } + 0 . 5 \mathrm { m m } ( t _ { n e t } + 0 . 0 2 \mathrm { i n . } ) } \end{array}$ and $t _ { n e t } + 1 . 0 \mathrm { m m } ( t _ { n e t } + 0 . 0 4 \mathrm { i n . } )$ , coating (applied in accordance with the coating manufacturer’s requirements) or annual gauging may be adopted as an alternative to steel renewal. Coating is to be maintained in condition with only minor spot rusting.

For the internal structure of double skin hatch covers, thickness gauging is required when hatch cover top or bottom plating renewal is to be carried out, or when this is deemed necessary , on the basis of the plating corrosion or deformation condition. In these cases, steel renewal for the internal structures is required where the gauged thickness is less than $t _ { n e t }$ mm (in.).

For corrosion addition $t _ { S } = 1 . 0 \mathrm { m m } ( 0 . 0 4 \mathrm { i n . } )$ the thickness for steel renewal is $t _ { n e t }$ mm (in.) and the thickness for coating or annual gauging is when gauged thickness is between $t _ { n e t }$ mm (in.) and $t _ { n e t } + 0 . 5 \mathrm { m m } ( t _ { n e t } + 0 . 0 2 \mathrm { i n . } )$

## 10 Hatchways Closed by Covers of Steel Fitted with Gaskets and Clamping Devices for Spaces Other Than Cargo Holds (2024)

## 10.1 Strength of Covers

## 10.1.1 Scantlings

Where weathertight covers are constructed of steel, the maximum allowable stress and deflection under the design loads in [3.3] and the minimum top plate thickness are as follows

Maximum allowable stress 0.8Y, and not to exceed the critical buckling strength in compression

Maximum allowable deflection 0.0056 times the span, which is the greatest span of the primary support members

Top plate thickness 0.01s, but not less than 6 mm (0.24 in.)

where Y and s are as defined in [9.1] and [9.3] , respectively.

Where the cross section of hatch cover stiffeners is not constant along the span, Appendix 3-2-A6 may be used to determine required scantlings.

## 10.3 Other Materials

The strength and stiffness of covers made of materials other than steel is to be equivalent to those of steel. Details for equivalency is to be submitted to ABS for approval.

## 10.5 Means for Securing Weathertightness

The covers are to be fitted with gaskets and clamping devices and so secured to maintain weathertightness in any sea conditions.

## 11 Hatchways in Decks at Higher Levels

## 11.1 Hatchways in Decks at Higher Levels (2024)

For the omission of gaskets on covers of hatchways in decks at high levels of cargo holds solely for transport of containers, see [9.19.2(b)] . For tests during subsequent surveys, refer to 7-3-2/1.1.1(f) and 7-3-2/5.1.11 of the ABS Rules for Survey After Construction (Part 7).

## 11.3 Hatchways in Lower Decks or within Fully Enclosed Superstructures

The following scantlings are intended for vessels of unrestricted service having conventional type covers. Scantlings for different types of covers or for vessels of restricted service will be separately considered.

## 11.3.1 Steel Covers (2024)

Where steel covers are fitted, the thickness of the plating is to be not less than required for platform decks in enclosed cargo spaces as obtained from 3-2-3/5.1. A stiffening bar is to be fitted around the edges as required to provide the necessary rigidity to permit the covers being handled without deformation. The effective depth of the framework is normally to be not less than 4% of its unsupported length. Each stiffener in association with the plating to which it is attached is to have section modulus not less than that obtained from the following equation:

$$
S M = 7. 8 h s \ell^ {2} \mathrm{cm} ^ {3}
$$

$$
S M = 0. 0 0 4 1 h s \ell^ {2} \mathrm{in} ^ {3}
$$

where

$h$ = $h _ { c s } ,$ in m (ft), the tween deck height for decks. Where the cargo uniform load pis specified and differs from 7.01 kN/m<sup>3</sup> (715 kgf/m<sup>3</sup>, 44.7 lbf/ft<sup>3</sup>) multiplied by the tween deck height, the height is to be proportionately adjusted.

S = spacing of the stiffeners, in m (ft)

= length of the stiffener, in m (ft)

## 11.3.2 Wheel Loading

Where provision is to be made for the operation or stowage of vehicles having rubber tires, the thickness of the hatch cover plating is to be not less than obtained from 3-2-3/5.17, for platform deck plating, except that the thickness of plate panels adjacent to the edges of the cover is to be at least 15% greater than that obtained from 3-2-3/5.17.

## 11.3.3 Beams and Wood Covers (2024)

Hatchways in lower decks or within fully enclosed superstructures are to be framed with steel beams of sufficient strength. Where such hatches are intended to carry a load of cargo, the hatch beams are to have a section modulus not less than that obtained from the following equation:

$$
S M = 7. 8 h s \ell^ {2} \mathrm{cm} ^ {3}
$$

$$
S M = 0. 0 0 4 1 h s \ell^ {2} \mathrm{in} ^ {3}
$$

where

```txt
c = 1.18
```

h = tween-deck height, in m (ft). When a design load is specified, is to be taken as $p / n$ where is the specified design pressure, in kN/m<sup>2</sup> (kgf/m<sup>2</sup>, lbf/ft<sup>2</sup>), and is defined as 7.01 (715, 44.7).

S = spacing of hatch beams, in m (ft)

l = length of hatch beams, in m (ft)

The wood covers are not to be less than 63.5 mm (2.50 in.) thick where the spacing of the beams does not exceed 1.52 m (5 ft). Where the height to which the cargo may be loaded on top of a hatch exceeds 2.6 m (8.5 ft), or where the spacing of the beams exceeds 1.52 m (5 ft), the thickness of the wood covers is to be suitably increased.

## 13 Small Hatches on the Exposed Fore Deck (1 July 2024)

The requirements of this Subsection are applicable to vessels with length, L, as defined in 3-1-1/3.1, of 80 m (263 feet) or more where the height of the exposed deck in way of the hatch is less than 0.1 or 22 m (72.2 ft) above the summer load waterline, whichever is less. The requirements apply to all small hatches located on the exposed fore deck within the forward 0.25 . Small hatches in the context of this Subsection are hatches designed for access to spaces below the deck and are capable of being closed weathertight or watertight, as applicable. Their opening is normally 2.5 m<sup>2</sup> (27 ft<sup>2</sup>) or less.

The requirements of this Subsection except that in 3-2-15/13.1 are not applicable to small hatches on container ships, which give access to a cargo hold and meet the conditions of 3-2-15/9.19.2(b). Hatch covers of such small hatches are considered non-weathertight regardless of whether they are actually weathertight or not. Such small hatches are to comply with the strength requirements in 3-2-15/13.1.

Hatches designed for emergency escape need not comply with [13.3i.] , [13.3ii.] , [13.5iii.] and [13.7] .

## 13.1 Strength (2024)

For small rectangular steel hatch covers, the plate thickness, stiffener arrangement and scantlings are to be in accordance with [TABLE 9] and [FIGURE 13] . Stiffeners, where fitted, are to be aligned with the metalto-metal contact points required in [13.5] (see also [FIGURE 13] ). Primary stiffeners are to be continuous. All stiffeners are to be welded to the inner edge stiffener (see [FIGURE 14] ).

## Note:

For hatch covers with nominal sizes between the dimensions indicated in [TABLE 9] , the stiffeners of the larger cover are to be required for stiffener scantling

In those cases where the proposed hatch cover is larger than those indicated in [TABLE 9] , but still in the range required to comply with this section (i.e., with opening of 2.5 square meters or less), the scantlings as indicated below are to be applied, with the stiffener arrangement similar to that indicated for hatch covers of 1330 x 1330 mm. Note that in no case are the scantlings to be less than those calculated in accordance with the requirements for the stiffeners of steel covers fitted with gaskets and clamping devices.

<table><tr><td>Nominal Size</td><td>Cover Plate Thickness</td><td>Primary Stiffeners</td><td>Secondary Stiffeners</td></tr><tr><td>(mm x mm)</td><td>(mm)</td><td colspan="2">Flat Bar (mm x mm); number</td></tr><tr><td>1580 x 1580</td><td>8</td><td>180 x 14; 2</td><td>100 x 10; 2</td></tr></table>

The upper edge of the hatchway coaming is to be suitably reinforced by a horizontal section, normally not more than 170 to 190 mm (6.9 to 7.5 in) from the upper edge of the coaming.

## Commentary:

The horizontal stiffener should have strength enough to resist the pressures as calculated by section 3-2-17/11.7.2, with allowable bending stress as defined in section 3-2-17/11.7.3(a).

In the calculation of the pressure for hatches of rectangular shape, it should consider $C _ { d } = 1 . 0$ and $C _ { p } = 1 . 0$ . The bending moment should be calculated considering the stiffener fixed at ends. A corrosion addition to the net section of 2. 0mm should be considered when defining the final stiffener's scantlings.

For small circular hatches in order to verify the scantlings of the horizontal stiffeners on the coaming, the hatch should be considered as a square with a side equal to the diameter of the offered circular hatch cover, and the same procedure applied for hatches of rectangular shape, but considering $C _ { d } = 0 . 8$ and $C _ { p } = 1 . 0$ in the calculation of the pressure.

End of Commentary

<!-- 原 PDF 第 401–600 页 -->

For small hatch covers of circular or similar shape, the cover plate thickness and reinforcement is to provide strength and stiffness equivalent to the requirements for small rectangular hatches.

For small hatch covers constructed of materials other than steel, the required scantlings are to provide strength and stiffness equivalent to 235 N/mm<sup>2</sup> (24 kgf/mm<sup>2</sup>, 34,000 psi) yield strength steel. Strength of small hatch covers constructed of aluminum alloy may be in accordance with [7.3] .

## 13.3 Primary Securing Devices (2024)

The primary securing devices are to be such, that their hatch covers can be secured in place and made weathertight by means of a mechanism employing any one of the following methods:

i) Butterfly nuts tightening onto forks (clamps), or

ii) Quick acting cleats, or

iii) A central locking device.

Dogs (twist tightening handles) with wedges are not acceptable.

## Commentary:

Securing devices of hatches designed for emergency escape should be of a quick-acting type (e.g., one action wheel handles are provided as central locking devices for latching/unlatching of hatch cover) operable from both sides of the hatch cover.

End of Commentary

Emergency escape hatches need not comply with i) and ii) above.

## 13.5 Requirements for Primary Securing (2024)

i) The hatch cover is to be fitted with a gasket of elastic material. This is to be designed to allow a metal-to-metal contact at a designed compression and to prevent over compression of the gasket by green sea forces that may cause the securing devices to be loosened or dislodged. The metal-to-metal contacts are to be arranged close to each securing device, in accordance with [FIGURE 14] , and of sufficient capacity to withstand the bearing force.

ii) The primary securing method is to be designed and manufactured such, that the designed compression pressure is achieved by one person without the need of any tools. A short bar for on/ off tilting of quick acting cleats is acceptable.

iii) For a primary securing method using butterfly nuts, the forks (clamps) are to be of robust design. They are to be designed to minimize the risk of butterfly nuts being dislodged while in use, by knuckling the forks’ tips upward, and raising the top surface on the free end, or by any similar method. The plate thickness of un-stiffened steel forks is not to be less than 16 mm . An example arrangement is shown in [FIGURE 14] . Emergency escape hatches need not comply with the forgoing requirements in this paragraph.

iv) For small hatch covers on the exposed deck forward of the superstructure or deckhouse, the hinges are to be fitted on the fore edge such that the predominant direction of green water will cause the cover to close.

v) For small hatch covers located on the exposed deck forward of the fore-most cargo hatch, the hinges are to be fitted such that the predominant direction of green sea will cause the cover to close, which means that the hinges are normally to be located on the fore edge.

vi) On small hatches located between the main hatches, for example, between Nos. 1 and 2, the hinges are to be placed on the fore edge or outboard edge, whichever is practicable for protection from green water in beam sea and bow quartering conditions.

vii) On small hatches located elsewhere the hinges are to be placed either on the fore edge or outboard edge, whichever is more practical for protection against green water coming from beam sea and/or bow quartering sea at their location.

## 13.7 Secondary Devices (2024)

Small hatches on the fore deck are to be fitted with an independent secondary securing device, e.g., by means of a sliding bolt, a hasp or a backing bar of slack fit, which is capable of keeping the hatch cover in place even in the event that the primary securing device became loosened or dislodged. It is to be fitted on the side opposite to the hatch cover hinges. Emergency escape hatches need not comply with the forgoing requirements in this paragraph.

## Commentary:

The secondary device does not necessarily need to keep the hatch cover weathertight.

End of Commentary

## 15 Other Hatchways

## 15.1 Hatchways within Open Superstructures

Hatchways within open superstructures are to be considered as exposed.

## 15.3 Hatchways within Deckhouses

Hatchways within deckhouses may be flush or are to have coamings and closing arrangements related to the degree of protection offered by the deckhouse itself, in terms of construction and the means provided for the closing of all external deckhouse openings.

## 17 Additional Requirements for Subdivision

## 17.1 External Opening below Damage Waterline (2024)

All external openings leading to compartments assumed intact in the damage analysis, which are permitted by 3-3-1/5.3 to be below the final damage waterline, are to be watertight. Except for cargo hatch covers, these openings are to be fitted with indicators on the bridge showing whether the closing appliances are open or closed.

## 17.3 Internal Openings

The openings and penetrations in internal decks required to be watertight for subdivision are to meet the corresponding requirements for watertight doors in 3-2-9/1.3 and 3-2-9/9.

## 19 Machinery Casings

## 19.1 Arrangement

Machinery-space openings in Position 1 or 2 are to be framed and efficiently enclosed by steel casings of ample strength, and, wherever practical, those openings in freeboard decks are to be located within superstructures or deckhouses. Where the machinery casings are exposed, plating and stiffeners are to be in accordance with the requirements in 3-2-11/3. Access openings in exposed casings are to be fitted with steel doors complying with the requirements of 3-2-11/5.3, the sills of which are to be at least 600 mm (23.5 in.) above the deck if in Position 1, and at least 380 mm (15 in.) above the deck if in Position 2. Where the vessel is assigned a freeboard less than that based on Table B as allowed by the International Convention on Load Lines, 1966, there are generally to be no openings giving direct access from the freeboard deck to the machinery space. A door, complying with the requirements of 3-2-11/5.3, may however be permitted in the exposed machinery casing, provided that it leads to a space or passageway that is as strongly constructed as the casing and is separated from the engine room by a second door complying with 3-2-11/5.3. The sill of the exterior door is not to be less than 600 mm (23.5 in.), and the sill of the second/interior door is to be not less than 230 mm (9 in.). Other openings in such casings are to be fitted with equivalent steel covers, permanently attached in their proper positions. See also 4-7-2/1.9.5 and 4-7-2/1.9.6.

## 19.3 Fiddleys, Funnels, and Ventilators

Coamings of any fiddley, funnel or machinery-space ventilator in an exposed position on the freeboard or superstructure deck are to be as high above the deck as reasonable and practicable. Fiddley openings are to be fitted with strong covers of steel or other equivalent material, permanently attached in their proper positions and capable of being secured weathertight.

## 19.5 Casings within Open Superstructures

Scantlings of casings within open superstructures are to be in compliance with 3-2-11/3 for exposed casings on superstructure decks. Where end bulkheads to the superstructures are not provided, the arrangements and scantlings of casings are to be in compliance with 3-2-11/3 for an exposed casing on the freeboard deck.

## 19.7 Casings within Enclosed Superstructures

The thickness of casings within enclosed superstructures is to be not less than obtained from the following equation:

$$
t = 4. 6 + L / 6 4 + (s - 7 6 0) / 1 5 0 \mathrm{mm}
$$

but not less than 6.0 mm

$$
t = 0. 1 8 1 + L / 5 3 3 3 + (s - 3 0) / 1 5 0 \mathrm{in}.
$$

but not less than 0.23 in.

The thickness of casing sides in accommodation spaces, above the crown of the machinery space, is not to be less than obtained from the following equation:

Where accelerated corrosion is expected, maybe such as in way of wet spaces, the thickness of coaming plates ought to be increased. Where casings are used in lieu of girders or deep beams, the plating in way of them is to be suitably increased. Stiffeners are to be fitted in line with the beams and are to have a section modulus not less than obtained from the following equation:

Casings which support girders or pillars are to be stiffened in such a manner as to provide supports not less effective than required for stanchions or pillars.

## 19.9 Casings within Deckhouses

Casings within deckhouses are to have scantlings, sill heights and closing arrangements to entrances related to the degree of protection offered by the deckhouse itself, in terms of construction and the means provided for closing of all external deckhouse openings.

S = spacing of stiffeners, in m (ft)

= height of casing, in m (ft)

= length, between supports, of the stiffeners, in m (ft)

## 21 Miscellaneous Openings in Freeboard and Superstructure Decks

## 21.1 Manholes and Scuttles

Manholes and flush scuttles in Position 1 or 2 or within superstructures other than enclosed superstructures are to be closed by covers capable of being made watertight. Unless secured by bolts spaced not more than 5 times the bolts’ diameter, the covers are to be permanently attached.

## 21.3 Other Openings

Openings in freeboard decks other than hatchways, machinery-space openings, manholes and flush scuttles are to be protected by an enclosed superstructure or by a deckhouse, or companionway of equivalent strength and weathertightness. Any such opening in an exposed superstructure deck or in the top of a deckhouse on the freeboard deck, which gives access to a space below the freeboard deck or a space within an enclosed superstructure, is to be protected by a deckhouse or companionway as well. Doorways in such deckhouses or companionways are to be fitted with doors complying with the requirements of 3-2-11/5.3.

## 21.5 Escape Openings

i) The closing appliances of escape openings are to be of a type that is operable from each side.

ii) The maximum force needed to open the hatch cover is not to exceed 150 N (15.3 kgf, 33.7 lbf).

iii) The use of a spring equalizing, counterbalance or other suitable device on the hinge side to reduce the force needed for opening is acceptable.

## 21.7 Companionway Sills (2022)

The height above the deck of sills to the doorways in companionways is to be as follows:

<table><tr><td>Position 1</td><td>Position 2</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">For vessels 24 meters (79 feet) in length and greater</td></tr><tr><td>600 mm (23.5 in.)</td><td>380 mm (15 in.)</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">For vessels under 24 meters (79 feet) in length $^{(1,2)}$ </td></tr><tr><td>450 mm (17.5 in.)</td><td>300 mm (12 in.)</td></tr></table>

## Notes:

1 Sill heights may be reduced on vessels which have freeboard in excess of the minimum geometric freeboard and/or a superstructure deck with height of deck in excess of the standard height of a superstructure.

2 For vessels with L < 24 m (79 ft), the sill height should be as indicated above, unless otherwise specifically requested by flag Administration.

## 21.9 Mast Openings

Openings penetrating decks and other structures to accommodate masts, kingposts and similar members are to be reinforced by fitting doublings or plating of increased thickness.

## 21.11 Chain Pipe Opening

Chain pipes through which anchor chains or wires are led are to be provided with permanently attached closing appliances minimizing the ingress of water. Steel, aluminum plate or a canvas cover with appropriate lashing arrangement will be acceptable for this purpose\*. A cement and wire mesh arrangement is not permitted.

The arrangement on vessels that are not subject to the International Convention on Load Lines or its Protocol may be specially considered.

Note: \* Examples of acceptable arrangements are such as:

i) Steel plates with cutouts to accommodate chain links or

ii) Canvas hoods with a lashing arrangement that maintains the cover in the secured position.

PART 3

C H A P T E R 2

Hull Structures and Arrangements

S E C T I O N 1 6

Protection of Shell Openings

## 1 General

## 1.1 Objective (2024)

1.1.1 Goals

The vessel structure is to be designed, constructed, operated, and maintained to:

<table><tr><td>Goal No.</td><td>Goal</td></tr><tr><td>STRU 1</td><td>In the intact conditions, have sufficient structural strength to withstand the environmental conditions, loading conditions, and operational loads anticipated during the design life.</td></tr><tr><td>STRU 2</td><td>Resist structural failure associated with accident conditions.</td></tr><tr><td>STRU 3</td><td>Provide protection to persons onboard, the environment and required safety services.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB 1</td><td>Have adequate watertight integrity and restoring energy to prevent capsize in an intact condition.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB 2</td><td>Have adequate subdivision and stability to provide survivability to damage or accidental conditions.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB 4</td><td>Detect accumulated liquids.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB 5</td><td>Be able to remove accumulated liquids to mitigate the effects of flooding.</td></tr><tr><td>MGMT 3</td><td>Establish procedures, plans and instructions for operations concerning the safety of the personnel, vessel, and protection of the environment. (ISM Code 7)</td></tr><tr><td>AUTO 4</td><td>Provide the equivalent degree of safety and operability from a remote location as those provided by local controls.</td></tr></table>

## 1.1.2 Functional Requirements

To achieve the above stated goals, the following functional requirements apply to this section:

<table><tr><td>Functional Requirement No.</td><td>Functional Requirements</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Stability (STAB)</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR1</td><td>Openings in the sides of the vessels are to be watertight and protected to prevent water ingress into the intact hull.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR2</td><td>The number of openings is to be minimized considering the operation of the vessel.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR3</td><td>Means to drain water are to be provided in case of water ingress through large openings and to prevent spread of any leakage water.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR4</td><td>The bow doors, inner doors, side shell doors and stern doors when fitted are to provide watertightness and structural integrity sufficient for their location, operational conditions and the surrounding structure.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR5</td><td>Provide remote visual surveillance of inaccessible locations that may be flooded by shell doors.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR6 (STRU)</td><td>Means are to be provided to prevent movement of the doors and accidental opening when closed.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Automation: Control, Monitoring and Safety Systems (AUTO)</td></tr><tr><td>AUTO-FR1</td><td>Means of controlling and monitoring doors and devices are to be provided at accessible local, and remote where applicable, locations with fail-safe design.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Structure (STRU)</td></tr><tr><td>STRU-FR1</td><td>Scantlings are to have sufficient strength to resist failure and excessive deformation associated with buckling and yielding when subjected to the loads anticipated throughout the service life, including bow impact load, slamming load, hydrodynamic lift and drag loads, vibration, load from rudders, propellers, and propulsion improvement devices.</td></tr><tr><td>STRU-FR2</td><td>The design of the termination of structural members is to be such as to prevent yielding or fatigue cracks.</td></tr><tr><td>STRU-FR3</td><td>The workmanship is to avoid discontinuities, misalignment and other harmful details that may lead to failure in service.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Safety Management (MGMT)</td></tr><tr><td>MGMT-FR1</td><td>Information is to be provided for safe operation and maintenance of the door during the service life.</td></tr></table>

The goals and functional requirements in cross-referenced Rules are to be met.

## 1.1.3 Compliance

A vessel is considered to comply with the goals and functional requirements within the scope of classification when the applicable prescriptive requirements are complied with or when an alternative arrangement has been approved. Refer to Part 1D, Chapter 2.

## 1.1.4 Application

Bow Doors and Inner Doors are to comply with the requirements of Section 3-2-16 for the arrangement, strength and securing of bow doors and inner doors leading to a complete or long enclosed superstructure, or to a long non-enclosed superstructure, where fitted to attain minimum bow height equivalence.

The requirements in this section are for two types of bow doors – Visor Doors and Side-Opening Doors. Other type of bow doors will be specially considered in association with the applicable requirements of these rules .

Side Shell Doors and Stern Doors are to comply with the requirements of Section 3-2-16 for the arrangement, strength and securing of side shell doors, abaft the collision bulkhead, and stern doors leading to enclosed spaces.

Side shell openings leading to relatively small enclosed watertight compartments (such as bunkering stations or passageways) are to comply with [2] if fitted with a second watertight door of equivalent strength and watertightness. Side shell openings leading into a relatively large cargo or similar compartment without a second watertight door are to comply with [3] .

## Commentary:

The requirements in this section cover bow doors, side and stern doors and other shell openings leading to enclosed spaces below the freeboard deck and in the enclosed superstructure. Shell Openings without closing devices above freeboard deck should be included in the progressive flooding points for both intact and damage stability calculations.

For other miscellaneous shell openings and penetrations, refer to the following Rule sections:

3-2-2/9 for structural compensation for openings in shell

4-6-4/3.3.4 for pipe penetration to shell

4-6-5/7.5, 3-2-4/19.1, 4-6-2/9.13 for sea chests and shell connections

● 4-8-1/5.3.3 for special hull penetrations

● Requirementsfor Air Lubrication System Installation for shell openings for air dispensers on the hull

End of Commentary

## 1.1.5 Drawing submission

Drawings with the following information are to be submitted for the external doors:

i) General arrangement plan indicating location of the bow door, inner door, side shell door and stern door

ii) Door arrangement plan indicating doors and adjacent ship structure, securing devices and supporting devices and door operating mechanism

iii) Structural plans of the doors

iv) Door details indicating securing devices, supporting devices, locking devices, sealing arrangements, weld details, material specifications

v) Hull structure in way of the doors and details of attachments of supporting devices

vi) Lines plan indicating areas of transverse, horizontal and vertical projections of the bow door to enable angles and to be determined

vii) Drawings of Indicator lights and audible alarms for the doors and securing and locking devices.

viii) Arrangement plan of water leakage detection system, alarm and television surveillance system.

ix) Operating and Maintenance Manual

x) Calculations for the door, securing devices and supporting devices.

Commentary:

The following statutory requirements and IACS documents can be taken as reference for external openings:

● ICLL Reg.21

SOLAS II-1/B-2/Reg. 15,15-1, 16

IACS UI LL21

IACS UR S8, S9, S15, S16, Z24

IACS UR Technical Background document

End of Commentary

## 2 Cargo, Gangway, or Fueling Ports

## 2.1 Construction (2024)

Cargo, gangway, or fueling ports in the sides ofvessels are to be capable ofbeing made thoroughly watertight. Where frames are cut in way of such ports, web frames are to be fitted on each side of the opening and arrangements are to be provided for the support of the beams over the opening. Thick insert plates are to be fitted in the side shell to compensate for the openings. Doubler plates are not allowed for vessels over 61 m (200 feet) in length. The corners of the openings are to be well rounded.

Unless otherwise specifically required, openings in the side shell are to have a minimum corner radius of 0.1 times the width of the opening but need not exceed 450 mm (18 in.). Additionally, the minimum radius in way of narrow vertical ligaments between adjacent openings having the same depth is not to be less than 150 mm (6 in.).

Waterway angles and scuppers are to be provided on the deck in way of openings in cargo spaces below the freeboard deck or in cargo spaces within enclosed superstructures, to prevent the spread of any leakage water over the cargo deck.

Indicators showing whether the ports in the side shell below the freeboard or superstructure deck are secured closed or open are to be provided on the navigation bridge. See 4-9-8/1.9.2 for the requirements.

All outer doors are to open outwards unless specially approved.

## Commentary:

IACS UI LL5 states that doors should generally open outwards to provide additional security against the impact of the sea. Doors which open inwards are subject to special approval by ABS.

For side or stern doors opening inwards, which in damaged condition can be immersed below equilibrium or intermediate waterplane, the deflections of the door frame should be controlled to not affect watertightness of the door. For the structural analysis for large doors, refer to the Commentary to [11.7] . Watertightness tests should be carried out in accordance wit [11.7] .

IACS UR S-9/S9.5.1 & S9.5.2 provide requirements for side shell door and stern doors opening inward.

## End of Commentary

## 2.3 Location (2024)

Unless especially approved, the lower edge of cargo, gangway, or fueling port openings is not to be below a line drawn parallel to the freeboard deck at side, which has at its lowest point at least 230 mm (9 in.) above the upper edge of the uppermost load line, including all assigned seasonal marks. See 3-2-16/FIGURE 1.

Cargo ports or similar openings having their lower edge below the line defined above are to be fitted with a second internal door of equivalent strength and water-tightness to the shell door, with a leakage detection device for the enclosed compartment between both doors. The drain from this compartment is to be led to the bilge with a screw-down valve, remotely controlled from an accessible location (see 4-6-4/3.3). Such ports are not to have their lowest point below the deepest subdivision loadline. (Passenger Vessel).

FIGURE 1 Location of Cargo, Gangway, or Fueling Port Openings (2024)  
![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/971076552f715e532efd9b50d739c3a6593bcfb73a0243fef12ec5c0c20fe071.jpg)  
Lower edge of cargo, gangway, or fueling port openings not allowed at this region

## 2.5 Watertight Subdivision Openings (2024)

For passenger ships and cargo ships of80 m in length and above, the relevant regulations concerning shell and watertight subdivision openings contained in SOLAS 1974 as amended are to be complied with. See [1.1.5] / Commentary. For non-SOLAS vessels, the requirements ofthe flag Administrations are to be complied with.

Openings in the shell plating below the deck, limiting the vertical extent of damage, are to be kept permanently closed while at sea. Should any of these openings be accessible during the voyage, their closing appliances are to be fitted with a device which prevents unauthorized opening.

Closing appliances which are kept permanently closed at sea to provide the watertight integrity of external openings but are not fitted with a device which prevents unauthorized opening, due to their inaccessibility during the voyage, are to be provided with a notice affixed to each such closing appliance to the effect that it is to be kept closed.

## 3 Bow Doors, Inner Doors, Side Shell Doors and Stern Doors

## 3.1 General (2024)

Bow doors requirements in 3-2-16/3 are for the arrangement of bow doors and inner doors leading to a complete or long forward enclosed superstructures, or to a long non-enclosed superstructure, where fitted to attain minimum bow height equivalence. Hull supporting structure in way of the bow doors is to be able to withstand the loads imposed by the bow door securing and supporting devices without exceeding the allowable stresses for those devices, both given in this section.

Side shell doors fitted abaft of the collision bulkhead and stern doors leading into enclosed spaces are to meet the requirements of this section.

## 3.3 Arrangement

## 3.3.1 General

As far as practicable, bow doors and inner doors are to be arranged so as to preclude the possibility of the bow door causing structural damage to the inner door or to the collision bulkhead n the case of damage to or detachment of the bow door.

## 3.3.2 Bow Doors

Bow doors are to be situated above the freeboard deck except that where a watertight recess fitted for arrangement of ramps or other related mechanical devices is located forward of the collision bulkhead and above the deepest waterline, the bow doors may be situated above the recess.

## 3.3.3 Inner Doors

An inner door is to be fitted in the extension of the collision bulkhead required by 3-2-9/3.1.1. A vehicle ramp made watertight and conforming to 3-2-9/3.3 FIGURE 1A in the closed position can be accepted for this purpose.

## 3.3.4 Side Shell and Stern Doors (2024)

Stern doors for passenger vessels are to be situated above the freeboard deck.

Stern doors for Ro-Ro cargo vessels and all side shell doors need not be situated above the freeboard deck. The location of the stern doors and side shell doors is to comply with [2.3] .

For vessels with large stern or side doors for equipment or cargo, the following are to be taken into consideration in the design:

When the doors are located below the vertical limit or need to be open at sea, two scenarios are to be considered for the enclosed spaces protected by the door in damage stability, considering the space open and closed for floating conditions.

In addition to [17] , the strength of the side and stern doors is to be equivalent to the strength of the surrounding structure. Scantlings of the doors can be determined based on direct strength calculations. See Section 3-2-20 for guidance on the direct analysis. All load transmitting elements in the design load path from the door through securing and supporting devices into the ship structure, including welded connection, are to be of the same strength standard as required for the securing and supporting devices.

## Commentary:

If compliance with [3.3.1] is not practicable, or inner door cannot be fitted in the extension of the collision bulkhead as required in [3.3.3] , a separate inner weathertight door should be installed.

## End of Commentary

## 5 Definitions (2024)

## 5.1 Definitions

## 5.1.1 Securing Device

A device used to keep the door closed by preventing it from rotating about its hinges or its pivoted attachments to the vessel.

## 5.1.2 Supporting Device

A device used to transmit external or internal loads from the door to a securing device and from the securing device to the vessel’s structure, or a device other than a securing device, such as a hinge, stopper or other fixed device, that transmits loads from the door to the vessel’s structure.

## 5.1.3 Locking Device

A device, which locks a securing device in the closed position.

## 5.1.4 Bow Door (2024)

Visor Doors. Opened by rotating upwards and outwards about a horizontal axis through two or more hinges located near the top of the door and connected to the primary structure of the door by longitudinal arranged lifting arms. See 3-2-16/FIGURE 2.

Side-opening Doors. Opened either by rotating outwards about a vertical axis through two or more hinges located near the outboard edges or by horizontal translation by means of linking arms arranged with pivoted attachments to the door and the ship. It is anticipated that side-opening bow doors are arranged in pairs. See 3-2-16/FIGURE 2.

FIGURE 2 Bow Door Type

## 7 Securing and Supporting Devices - Arrangements (2024)

## 7.1 General

Securing and supporting devices are to be arranged in accordance with this subsection, and are to have scantlings as required by [13.9] , [15.5] or [17.9] as appropriate.

## 7.3 Side Shell and Stern Doors (2024)

Means are to be provided to prevent lateral or vertical movement of the side shell or stern doors when closed. Means are also to be provided for mechanically fixing the doors in the open position. See 3-2-16/FIGURE 3 for cleating hook and wedge arrangement.

The means of securing and supporting the doors are to have strength and stiffness equivalent to the adjacent structure.

Clearance and packing for side shell and stern doors are to be in accordance with [7.5.1] .

![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/982934779171850f4117841af48f26e9a68e3aa56cfe2be347308974b993399c.jpg)

# FIGURE 3 Example Cleat Arrangement (2024)

Cleating Hook

## 7.5 Bow Doors (2024)

Means are to be provided to prevent lateral or vertical movement of the bow doors when closed. Means are also to be provided for mechanically fixing the door in the open position. See [FIGURE 3] .

Means of securing and supporting the door are to maintain equivalent strength and stiffness of the adjacent structure.

## 7.5.1 Clearance and Packing

The maximum design clearance between the door and securing/supporting devices is not to exceed 3 mm (0.12 in.). Where packing is fitted, it is to be of a comparatively soft type and the supporting forces are to be carried by the steel structure only.

## 7.5.2 Visor Door Arrangement (2024)

The pivot arrangement is to be such that the visor is self-closing under external loads. The closing moment, $M _ { y } ,$ as defined in [19.5.1] is not to be less than $M _ { y o }$ as given by the following equation:

$$
M _ {y o} = W _ {c} + 0. 1 \sqrt {a ^ {2} + b ^ {2}} \sqrt {F _ {x} ^ {2} + F _ {z} ^ {2}}
$$

where W, a, b, c, $F _ { x }$ and $F _ { z }$ are as defined in [17] .

In addition, the arrangement of the door is to be such that the reaction forces of pin or wedge supports at the base of the door does not act in the forward direction when the door is loaded in accordance with [19.5.4] .

## Commentary:

The intention of the requirements in 3-2-16/7.5.2 for pivot or hinge arrangement is that the door is effectively selfclosing under external loads, and the opening moment is to be balanced by the reaction forces.

## End of Commentary

## Securing and Locking Arrangement

## 9.1 General

Securing devices are to be provided with a mechanical locking arrangement (self-locking or separate arrangement), or are to be of the gravity type.

## 9.3 Operation (2024)

Securing devices are to be simple to operate and readily accessible. The opening and closing systems as well as the securing and locking devices are to be interlocked in such a way that they can only operate in the proper sequence.

For control and monitoring of securing devices, water leakage protection and door surveillance, refer to [4-9-8/1.7] and 4-9-8/1.9.

## 11 Tightness

## 11.1 Bow Doors (2024)

Bow doors are to be so fitted as to provide tightness and to give effective protection to the inner doors.

## 11.3 Inner Doors

Inner doors forming part of the extension of the collision bulkhead are to be weathertight over the full height of the cargo space and arranged with fixed sealing supports on the aft side of the doors.

## 11.5 Side Shell and Stern Doors

Side shell doors and stern doors are to provide water tightness.

## 11.7 Testing at Watertight Door Manufacturer (2024)

To comply with relevant subdivision and damage stability regulations, doors which become immersed by an equilibrium or intermediate waterplane at any stage of assumed flooding are to be hydrostatically tested at the manufacturer’s plant. The head of water used for the test shall correspond at least to the head measured from the lower edge of the door opening, at the location in which the door is to be fitted in the vessel, to the most unfavorable damage waterplane.

## Commentary:

For large doors greater than 6 m<sup>2</sup>, structural analysis may be accepted in lieu of pressure testing. Where such doors utilize gasket seals, a prototype pressure test of the gasket seal should be carried out to confirm that the compression of the gasket material can accommodate maximum deflection, as determined by the structural analysis. After installation of such a door, the initial gasket compression is to be recorded. Refer to SOLAS II-1/Reg.16/2 and UI 21.5.2 of MSC.1/Circ 1572 for doors where testing is not feasible.

## End of Commentary

## 13 Bow Door Scantlings

## 13.1 General

Bow doors are to be framed and stiffened so that the whole structure is equivalent to the intact bow structure when closed.

## 13.3 Primary Structure (2024)

Scantlings of primary members are to be designed so that the allowable stresses indicated in [25.1] are not exceeded when the structure is subjected to the design loads indicated in [19.1] . Normally, simple beam theory may be applied to determine the bending stresses. Members are to be considered to have simply supported end connections. The buckling strength of primary members is to be verified as being adequate. Refer to 3-2-20/9.3.

## 13.5 Secondary Stiffeners (2024)

Secondary stiffeners are to be supported by primary members constituting the main stiffening of the door. The section modulus, SM, of secondary stiffeners is to be as required 3-2-5/1.2 and 3-2-5/5. Consideration is to be given, where necessary, to differences in fixity between the requirements in 3-2-5/1.2, 3-2-5/5, and bow door stiffeners.

In addition, stiffener webs are to have a net sectional area exclusive of any openings, A, including effective brackets where applicable, not less than that obtained from the following equation:

$$
A = V Q / 1 0 \mathrm{cm} ^ {2} (A = V Q \mathrm{cm} ^ {2}, A = V Q / 6. 5 \mathrm{in} ^ {2})
$$

## where

V = shear force, in kN (tf, Ltf), in the stiffener calculated using the uniformly distributed external pressure, $P _ { e b } ,$ given in [19.1]

Q = as defined in 3-2-1/5.3.

## Commentary:

The term ”net sectional area” refers to the deduction of area due to openings in the web. A corrosion allowance does not need to be deducted.

For secondary stiffeners, if the fixity of the stiffeners at ends is simply supported, then SM should be adjusted by 1.5 times that required by Section 3-2-5, which assumes fixed-fixed

## End of Commentary

## 13.7 Plating

The thickness of bow door plating is to be not less than that required for side shell plating at the same location.

## 13.9 Securing and Supporting Devices – Scantlings for Bow Doors (2024)

Scantlings of securing and supporting devices are to be designed so that the allowable stresses indicated in [25.1] are not exceeded when the structure is subjected to the design loads indicated in [19.3] . All loadtransmitting elements in the design load path from the door through securing and supporting devices into the vessel structure, including welded connections, are to meet the strength standards required for securing and supporting devices. These elements include pins, support brackets and back-up brackets. Where fitted, threaded bolts are not to carry support forces, and the maximum tensile stress in way of the threads is not to exceed the allowable stress given in [25.5] .

In determining the required scantlings, the door is to be assumed to be a rigid body. Only those active supporting and securing devices having an effective stiffness in the relevant direction are to be included and considered when calculating the reaction forces on the devices. Small or flexible devices such as cleats intended to provide compression load on the packing material are not to be included in the calculations.

## 13.9.1 Bearing Pressure

The bearing pressure on steel to steel bearings is to be calculated by dividing the design force by the projected bearing area, and is not to exceed the allowable stress given in [25.3] .

## 13.9.2 Redundancy

In addition to the above requirements, the arrangement of the securing and supporting devices is to be designed with redundancy such that in the event of failure of any single securing or supporting device, the stresses in the remaining devices do not exceed the allowable stresses indicated in [25.1] by more than 20% when the above loads are applied.

## 13.9.3 Visor Door Securing and Supporting Devices

Securing and supporting devices, excluding the hinges, are to be capable of resisting the vertical design force given in [19.5.3] without exceeding the allowable stresses in [25.1] .

Two securing devices are to be provided at the lower part of the door, each capable of providing the full reaction force required to prevent opening of the door without stresses exceeding the allowable stresses indicated in [25.1] . The opening moment, M<sub>o</sub>, to be balanced by this force is as given in [19.5.2] .

## 13.9.4 Side-opening Door Thrust Bearing (2024)

A thrust bearing is to be provided in way of girder ends at the closing of the two doors, and is to prevent one door from shifting towards the other one under the effect of unsymmetrical pressure. Securing devices are to be fitted to secure sections thrust bearing to one another. See 3-2-16/Figure 4 for an example.

FIGURE 4 Example Thrust Bearing (2024)  
![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/d4f22d82734550f642e69651b182a8eee2bb5bbf1849a9c3deae1edd06a1a37c.jpg)

## 13.11 Visor Door Lifting Arms and Supports

Where visor type bow doors are fitted, calculations are to be submitted verifying that lifting arms and their connections to the door and vessel structure are adequate to withstand the static and dynamic forces applied during the lifting and lowering operations under a wind pressure of at least 1.5 kN/m<sup>2</sup> (0.15 tf/m<sup>2</sup>, 0.014 Ltf/ft.<sup>2</sup> ).

## 15 Inner Door Scantlings

## 15.1 General

Scantlings of inner doors are to meet the requirements of this subsection. In addition, where inner doors are used as vehicle ramps, scantlings are not to be less than required for vehicle decks in 3-2-3, 3-2-7, and 3-2-8.

## 15.3 Primary Structure (2024)

Scantlings of primary members are to be designed so that the allowable stresses indicated in [25.1] are not exceeded when the structure is subjected to the design loads indicated in [21.1] . The buckling strength of primary members is to be verified as being adequate. Refer to 3-2-20/9.3.

Plating and stiffeners of the inner door are to be equivalent to the intact bow structure when closed.

## 15.5 Securing and Supporting Devices

Scantlings of securing and supporting devices are to be designed so that the allowable stresses indicated in [25.1] are not exceeded when the structure is subjected to the design loads indicated in [21] . Where fitted, threaded bolts are not to carry support forces, and the maximum tensile stress in way of the threads is not to exceed the allowable stress given in [25.5] .

The bearing pressure on steel to steel bearings is to be calculated by dividing the design force by the projected bearing area, and is not to exceed the allowable stress given in [25.3] .

## 17 Side Shell Door and Stern Door Scantlings

## 17.1 General

Scantlings of side shell doors or stern doors are to meet the requirements of this subsection. In addition, where the doors are used as vehicle ramps, scantlings are not to be less than required for vehicle decks in 3-2-3, 3-2-7, and 3-2-8.

## 17.3 Primary Structure (2024)

Scantlings of primary members are to be designed so that the allowable stresses indicated in [25.1] are not exceeded when the structure is subjected to the design loads indicated in [23] . Normally, simple beam theory may be applied to determine the bending stresses. Members are considered to have simply supported end connections. The buckling strength of primary members is to be verified as being adequate. Refer to 3-2-20/9.3.

## 17.5 Secondary Stiffeners

Secondary stiffeners are to be supported by primary members constituting the main stiffening of the door. The section modulus, SM, of secondary stiffeners is to be not less than required by 3-2-5 for frames in the same location. In addition, the net sectional area of stiffener webs is to be in accordance with [13.5] , using the external pressure, $p _ { e } ,$ given in [23] .

## 17.7 Plating

The thickness of side or stern door plating is to be not less than that required for side shell plating at the same location.

## 17.9 Securing and Supporting Devices

Scantlings of securing and supporting devices are to be designed so that the allowable stresses indicated in [25.1] are not exceeded when the structure is subjected to the design loads indicated in [23] . All loadtransmitting elements in the design load path from the door through securing and supporting devices into the vessel structure, including welded connections, are to meet the strength standards required for securing and supporting devices. Where fitted, threaded bolts are not to carry support forces, and the maximum tensile stress in way of the threads is not to exceed the allowable stress given in [25.5] .

In determining the required scantlings, the door is to be assumed to be a rigid body. Only those active supporting and securing devices having an effective stiffness in the relevant direction are to be included and considered when calculating the reaction forces on the devices. Small or flexible devices such as cleats intended to provide compression load on the packing material are not to be included in the calculations.

## 17.9.1 Bearing Pressure

The bearing pressure on steel-to-steel bearings is to be calculated by dividing the design force by the projected bearing area, and is not to exceed the allowable stress given in [25.3] .

## 17.9.2 Redundancy

In addition to the above requirements, the arrangement of the securing and supporting devices is to be designed with redundancy such that in the event of a failure of any single securing or supporting device, the stresses in the remaining devices do not exceed the allowable stresses indicated in [25.1] by more than 20% under the above loads.

## 19 Bow Door Design Loads

## 19.1 External Pressure

The design external pressure, $P _ { e b } ,$ is to be taken as indicated by the following equation:

$$
P _ {e b} = n c (0. 2 2 + 0. 1 5 \mathrm{tan} \beta) (0. 4 V _ {d} \mathrm{sin} a + 0. 6 \sqrt {k L _ {1}}) ^ {2} \mathrm{kN/m} ^ {2} (\mathrm{tf/m} ^ {2}, \mathrm{Ltf/ft} ^ {2})
$$

where

n = 2.75 (0.280, 0.0256)

c 1.0

$L$ = length of vessel, as defined in 3-1-1/3.1, in m (ft.)

$L _ { I }$ = length of vessel, in m (ft.), as defined in 3-1-1/3.1, but need not be taken as greater than 200 m (656 ft.)

$\beta$ = flare angle at the point to be considered, defined as the angle between a vertical line and the tangent to the side shell plating measured in a vertical plane normal to the horizontal tangent to the shell plating. See [FIGURE 1] .

$\alpha$ = entry angle at the point to be considered, defined as the angle between a longitudinal line parallel to the centerline and the tangent to the shell plating in a horizontal plane. See [FIGURE 1] .

$k$ = 1.0 (1.0, 0.305)

$V _ { d }$ = vessel design speed, as defined in 3-2-14/3.1.

## 19.3 External Forces (2024)

The design external forces considered in determining scantlings of securing and supporting devices of bow doors are not to be taken less than those given by the following equations:

$$
F _ {x} = P _ {e m} A _ {x}
$$

$$
F _ {y} = P _ {e m} A _ {y}
$$

$$
F _ {z} = P _ {e m} A _ {z}
$$

where

$F _ { x }$ = the design external force in the longitudinal direction, in kN (tf, Ltf)

$F _ { y }$ = the design external force in the transverse direction, in kN (tf, Ltf)

$F _ { z }$ = the design external force in the vertical direction, in kN (tf, Ltf)

$A _ { x }$ = area, in $\mathrm { m } ^ { 2 } ( \mathrm { f t } ^ { 2 } ) ,$ of the transverse projection of the door between the levels of the bottom of the door and the top of the upper deck bulwark or between the bottom of the door and the top of the door, whichever is the lesser. Where the flare angle of the bulwark is at least $1 5 ^ { \circ }$ less than the flare of the adjacent shell plating, the bulwark may be excluded and the distance may be measured from the bottom of the door to the upper deck or to the top of the door, whichever is the lesser.

$A _ { y }$ = area, in $\mathbf { m } ^ { 2 } \left( \mathbf { f } \mathbf { t } ^ { 2 } \right)$ , of the longitudinal projection of the door between the levels of the bottom of the door and the top of the upper deck bulwark or between the bottom of the door and the top of the door, whichever is the lesser. Where the flare angle of the bulwark is at least $1 5 ^ { \circ }$ less than the flare of the adjacent shell plating, the bulwark may be excluded and the distance may be measured from the bottom of the door to the upper deck or to the top of the door, whichever is the lesser.

$A _ { z }$ = area, in $\mathbf { m } ^ { 2 } \left( \mathbf { f } \mathbf { t } ^ { 2 } \right)$ , of the horizontal projection of the door between the levels of the bottom of the door and the top of the upper deck bulwark or between the bottom of the door and the top of the door, whichever is the lesser. Where the flare angle of the bulwark is at least $1 5 ^ { \circ }$ less than the flare of the adjacent shell plating, the bulwark may be excluded and the distance may be measured from the bottom of the door to the upper deck or to the top of the door, whichever is the lesser.

$P _ { e m }$ = bow door pressure, $P _ { e b } ,$ determined using $\alpha _ { m }$ and $\beta _ { m }$ in place of α and $\beta .$

$\beta _ { m }$ = lare angle measured at a point on the bow door ℓ/2 aft of the stem line on a plane h/2 above the bottom of the door, as shown in [FIGURE 2] .

$\textit { a } _ { m }$ = entry angle measured at the same point as $\beta _ { m } .$ See [FIGURE 2] .

$h$ = height, in m (ft.), of the door between the levels of the bottom of the door and the upper deck or between the bottom of the door and the top of the door, whichever is less

ℓ = fore and aft length, in m (ft.), of the door at a height h/2 above the bottom of the door

## 19.5 Visor Door Forces, Moments and Load Cases

## 19.5.1 Closing Moment

For visor doors, the closing moment, $M _ { y }$ is to be taken as indicated by the following equation:

$$
M _ {y} = F _ {x} a + W c - F _ {z} b \mathrm{kN-m(tf-m,Ltf-ft.)}
$$

where

$W$ = weight of the visor door, in kN (tf, Ltf)

α 二 vertical distance, in m (ft), from the visor pivot to the centroid of the transverse vertical projected area of the visor door. See [FIGURE 3] .

$^ { b }$ = horizontal distance, in m (ft), from visor pivot to the centroid of the horizontal projected area of the visor door. See [FIGURE 3] .

c = horizontal distance, in m (ft), from the visor pivot to the center of gravity of the visor. See [FIGURE 3] .

$F _ { x }$ and $F _ { z }$ are as defined in [19.3]

## 19.5.2 Opening Moment

The opening moment, $M _ { o } ,$ is to be taken as indicated by the following equation:

$$
M _ {o} = W d + 5 A _ {x} a \mathrm{kN} - \mathrm{m} (W d + 0. 5 A _ {x} a \mathrm{tf} - \mathrm{m}, W d + 0. 0 4 7 A _ {x} a \mathrm{Ltf} - \mathrm{ft})
$$

where

d = vertical distance, in m (ft), from the hinge axis to the center of gravity of the door

W, A and a are as indicated above.

## 19.5.3 Vertical Design Force

The vertical design force is to be taken as $F _ { z } - W$ where $F _ { z }$ is as defined in [19.3] and $W$ is as defined in [19.5.1] .

## 19.5.4 Combined Load Case 1

The visor doors are to be evaluated under a load of $F _ { x } , F _ { z }$ and $W$ acting simultaneously with $F _ { x }$ and $F _ { z }$ acting at the centroid of their respective projected areas.

## 19.5.5 Combined Load Case 2

The visor doors are to be evaluated under a load of 0.7F<sub>y</sub> acting on each side separately together with $0 . 7 F _ { x } , 0 . 7 F _ { z }$ and $W , F _ { x } , F _ { y }$ and $F _ { z }$ are to be taken as acting at the centroid of their respective projected areas.

## 19.7 Side-Opening Door Load Cases

## 19.7.1 Combined Load Case 1

Side opening doors are to be evaluated under a load of $F _ { x } , F _ { y } , F _ { z }$ and $W$ acting simultaneously with $F _ { x } , F _ { y }$ and $F _ { z }$ acting at the centroid of their respective projected areas.

## 19.7.2 Combined Load Case 2

Side opening doors are to be evaluated under a load of 0.7F<sub>x</sub>, 0.7F<sub>x</sub> and W acting on both doors simultaneously and $0 . 7 F _ { y }$ acting on each door separately.

## 21 Inner Door Design Loads

## 21.1 External Pressure

The design external pressure is to be taken as the greater of $P _ { e i }$ or $P _ { h }$ as given by the following equations:

$$
P _ {e i} = 0. 4 5 \mathrm{L} 1 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} ^ {2} \left(0. 0 4 6 L _ {1} \mathrm{tf} / \mathrm{m} ^ {2}, 0. 0 0 1 2 8 L _ {1} \mathrm{Ltf} / \mathrm{ft} ^ {2}\right)
$$

$$
P _ {h} = 1 0 \mathrm{h} \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} ^ {2} (1. 0 h \mathrm{tf} / \mathrm{m} ^ {2}, 0. 0 2 9 h \mathrm{Ltf} / \mathrm{ft} ^ {2})
$$

where

$L _ { \mathrm { ~ l ~ } }$ is as defined in [19.1] .

h = the distance, in m (ft), from the load point to the top of the cargo space.

## 21.3 Internal Pressure

The design internal pressure, P is to be taken as not less than 25 kN/m<sup>2</sup> (2.5 tf/m<sup>2</sup>, 0.23 Ltf/ft<sup>2</sup>).

## 25.3 Steel Securing and Supporting Devices Bearing Stress

For steel to steel bearings in securing and supporting devices, the nominal bearing pressure is not to exceed $0 . 8 \sigma _ { f }$ , where $\sigma _ { f }$ is the yield stress of the bearing material.

## 25.5 Tensile Stress on Threaded Bolts

The tensile stress in threaded bolts is not to exceed 125/Q N/mm<sup>2</sup> (12.7/Q kgf/mm<sup>2</sup>, 18000/Q psi).

## 27 Operating and Maintenance Manual

The following information is to be submitted for review.

## 27.1 Manual

An operating and maintenance manual for the doors is to be provided onboard and is to contain at least the following:

Main particulars and design drawings

● Service conditions, e.g., service area restrictions, emergency operations, acceptable clearances for supports

● Maintenance and function testing

Register of inspections and repairs

## 27.3 Operating Procedures

Documented operating procedures for closing and securing the doors are to be kept onboard and posted at an appropriate location.

# Bulwarks, Rails, Freeing Ports, Side Scuttles, Windows, Ventilators, Tank Vents and Overflows (2024)

## 1 General (2024)

## 1.1 Objective

## 1.1.1 Goals

The vessel structure is to be designed, constructed, operated, and maintained to:

<table><tr><td>Goal No.</td><td>Goal</td></tr><tr><td>STAB 1</td><td>have adequate watertight integrity and restoring energy to prevent capsize in an intact condition.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB 5</td><td>be able to remove accumulated liquids to mitigate the effects of flooding.</td></tr><tr><td>STRU 1</td><td>in the intact condition, have sufficient structural strength to withstand the environmental conditions, loading conditions, and operational loads anticipated during the design life.</td></tr><tr><td>STRU 3</td><td>provide protection to persons onboard, environment and required safety service.</td></tr><tr><td>SAFE 1.2</td><td>provide means to minimize the risk of strikes against objects, slips, and falls within the vessel and overboard.</td></tr></table>

## 1.1.2 Functional Requirements

To achieve the above stated goals, the following functional requirements apply to this section:

<table><tr><td>Functional Requirement No.</td><td>Functional Requirements</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Safety of Personnel (SAFE)</td></tr><tr><td>SAFE-FR1</td><td>Efficient means are to be provided on all exposed parts of the freeboard and superstructure decks to which crew have normal access to prevent persons from falling overboard.</td></tr><tr><td>SAFE-FR2</td><td>Satisfactory means are to be provided for the protection of the crew from fire and heavy weather when transiting to and from their quarters, the machinery space and all other parts used during the normal operations of the ship.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Stability (STAB)</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR1</td><td>Where wells are formed on the weather portions of freeboard or superstructure decks, ample provision is to be made for rapidly freeing the decks of water.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR2 (STRU)</td><td>Side scuttles, windows, skylights, etc., including the glass, deadlights and storm covers, if fitted, are to be of substantial strength to provide watertightness/weathertightness of the external boundary.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR3</td><td>The position and size of the side scuttles and windows are to minimize the risk of water ingress.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR4</td><td>Ventilators and air pipes, tank vents and overflows are to be of substantial construction and be effectively protected to prevent water ingress.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR5</td><td>Means of closure are to be provided for openings in locations likely to have water on deck in heavy weather.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR6</td><td>Continuous supply of ventilation is to be provided to machinery and other critical spaces in heavy weather while minimizing the risk of water ingress.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR7</td><td>Automatic weathertight means are to be provided on air pipes to allow passage of air but prevent water ingress in all normal and emergency conditions.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR8</td><td>The intact and damage stability analysis is to consider the risk of water ingress through external openings leading to compartments.</td></tr></table>

## 1.1.3 Compliance

A vessel is considered to comply with the goals and functional requirements within the scope of classification when the applicable prescriptive requirements are complied with or when an alternative arrangement has been approved. Refer to Part 1D, Chapter 2.

## 2 Bulwarks and Guard Rails (2024)

The vessel is to be fitted either with permanent bulwarks or with efficient rails of the same height and of strong construction meeting requirements in this section, protecting all exposed parts of the freeboard and superstructure decks to which crew have normal access.

## 2.1 Height on Manned Vessels

The height of bulwarks and guard rails on exposed parts of freeboard and superstructure decks, and if applicable, at the boundary of first tier deckhouses and at the ends of superstructures is to be at least 1.0 m (39.5 in.) from the deck surface. Where this height would interfere with the operation of the vessel, a lesser height may be approved if adequate protection is provided. Where approval of a lower height is requested, justifying information is to be submitted.

## 2.3 Bulwarks (2024)

## 2.3.1 Strength Requirements (2024)

i) Bulwarks are to be of ample strength in proportion to their height and efficiently stiffened at the upper edge by a suitable bar or equivalent. The bulwark plating is to be kept clear of the sheerstrake and the lower edge effectively stiffened. Bulwarks and stays are to be aligned with underdeck structure.

The gross thickness of bulwark plating, at the boundaries of exposed freeboard deck and superstructure deck, is not to be less than that given in 3-2-17/Table 1A.

## TABLE 1A Thickness of Bulwark Plates

<table><tr><td>Height of bulwark</td><td>Gross Thickness of Bulwark Plate</td></tr><tr><td>1.8 m (5.91 ft) or more</td><td>Thickness required for a superstructure side in the same position, obtained from 3-2-11/3.3, but not less than 6 mm (0.24 in.).</td></tr><tr><td>1.0 m (3.28 ft)</td><td>6 mm (0.24 in.)</td></tr><tr><td>Intermediate Height</td><td>By linear interpolation</td></tr></table>

iii) Bulwarks are to be supported by efficient stays. Stays on freeboard decks are to be spaced not more than 1.83 m (6 ft) apart. The stays are to be formed either of flanged plate or builtup sections and are to be efficiently attached to the bulwarks and deck plating. The gross section modulus of stays, $Z _ { s t a y - g r }$ , is not to be less than:

$$
Z _ {\mathrm{stay-gr}} = 7 7 h _ {\mathrm{blwk}} ^ {2} S _ {\mathrm{stay}} \left(\mathrm{cm} ^ {3}\right),
$$

$$
Z _ {\mathrm{stay-gr}} = 0. 1 3 3 h _ {\mathrm{blwk}} ^ {2} S _ {\mathrm{stay}} \left(\mathrm{in} ^ {3}\right),
$$

where:

= height of bulwark from the top of the deck plating to the top of the rail, in m (ft).

= spacing of the stays, in m (ft).

In the calculation of the section modulus, only the material connected to the deck is to be included. The bulb or flange of the stay may be taken into account where connected to the deck.

Where the bulwark plating is connected to the sheer strake, a width of attached plating, not exceeding 600 mm (23.6 in.), may also be included.

iv) Where it is intended to carry timber deck cargoes, the bulwark stays are to be not more than 1.52 m (5 ft) apart and have increased attachment to deck and bulwark.

v) Gangways and other openings in bulwarks are to be located well away from breaks of superstructures, and heavy plates are to be fitted in way of mooring pipes.

vi) For vessels over 61 m (200 ft) in length, bulwarks are to be arranged such that they are free from hull girder stress within 0.6L amidships. Long bulwarks within 0.6L amidships are not to be welded to deck plating unless expansion joints are arranged at 0.1L apart.

## Commentary:

For vessels under 61 meters (200 ft) in length, bulwark plating on freeboard deck may be connected to the sheerstrake, provided the conditions listed below are complied with:

i The hull girder stress at the top of the bulwark, as well as at the deck at side, comply with the Rule required value.

ii The bulwark plate thickness is not less than thickness required for forecastle side plating.

iii Welding of bulwark plate to sheerstrake is carried out in accordance with Section [2-4-1] .

## End of Commentary

17 Bulwarks, Rails, Freeing Ports, Side Scuttles, Windows, Ventilators, Tank Vents and Overflows

## 2.3.2 Openings in Bulwarks (2024)

Openings in bulwarks are to be protected by rails or bars spaced not more than 230 mm (9 in.) apart. Vertical rails or bars spaced not more than 230 mm (9 in.) apart can be accepted in lieu of rails or bars arranged horizontally.

## 2.5 Guard Rails

2.5.1

Fixed, removable or hinged stanchions are to be fitted at approximately 1.5 m (5 ft) apart. Removable or hinged stanchions are to be capable of being locked in the upright position.

## 2.5.2 (1 July 2021)

At least every third stanchion is to be supported by a bracket or stay. Dimensions and arrangement of stanchion and stays are to be as shown in [FIGURE 2] . Where this arrangement would interfere with the safe traffic of persons on board, the following alternative arrangements of stanchions may be acceptable:

i) At least every third stanchion is to be of increased breadth, $k b _ { s } = 2 . 9  { b _ { s } }$ at the attachment of stanchion to the deck, or,

ii) At least every second stanchion is to be of increased breadth, $k b _ { s } = 2 . 4 \ : b _ { s }$ at the attachment of stanchion to the deck, or,

iii) Every stanchion is to be of increased breadth, $k b _ { s } = 1 . 9 b _ { s }$ at the attachment of stanchion to the deck.

where, $b _ { s }$ is not to be taken as less than 60 mm (2.36 in.) (see [FIGURE 3] ). The thickness of the flat bar stanchions is not to be less than 15 mm (0.59 in.).

For any of the above arrangements i), ii) or iii) above, the following details are to be complied with:

iv) Flat steel stanchion required by i), ii) or iii) above is to be aligned with supporting member below the deck unless the deck plating thickness exceeds 20 mm (0.79 in.) and welded to deck with double continuous fillet weld with minimum leg size of 7.0 mm (0.28 in.) or as specified by the design standard.

v) The underdeck supporting member of the stanchion is to be a minimum of 100 × 12 mm (4.0 × 0.5 in.) flat bar welded to deck by double continuous fillet weld (see [FIGURE 3] ).

Alternative arrangements could be acceptable provided that it can be shown equivalent in strength and stiffness to the above requirements or based on recognized international standards.

Lengths of chain may only be accepted in lieu of guard rails if they are fitted between two fixed stanchions and/or bulwarks.

Where necessary for the normal operation of the vessel, steel wire ropes may be accepted in lieu of guard rails. They may be used with either fixed or portable stanchions and shall be made taut by means of turnbuckles.

The clear opening below the lowest course is not to exceed 230 mm (9 in.). Where a foot-stop is installed at the deck level the clear opening below the lowest course may be measured from the top of the foot-stop. The clear distances between the lowest and the middle courses, as well as the middle and the upper courses are not to exceed 380 mm (15 in.).

## 2.5.4 (2019)

For vessels with rounded gunwales, stanchions are to be placed on the flat of the deck.

## 2.5.5 (2024)

Stanchions, rails and stays are to be provided with a protective coating.

Commentary:

Where the height of bulwarks or guard rails would interfere, at least half the length of the exposed parts of the freeboard deck should be fitted with open rails as per IACS UI LL59. Otherwise, freeing ports should be provided complying with [5] .

End of Commentary

## 3 Access and Crew Protection

## 3.1 General (2024)

Satisfactory means in the form of guard rails, lifelines, gangways or under-deck passages, etc., are to be provided for the protection of the crew in getting to and from their quarters, the machinery space, and all other parts (see [TABLE 1]).

## 3.3 Access to Bow on Tankers (2024)

Tankers, including oil carriers, fuel oil carriers, gas carriers and chemical carriers, are to be provided with means to enable the crew to gain safe access to the bow even in severe weather conditions in accordance with 3-2-17/Table 1B.
