## 4 Buckling Requirements for Direct Strength Analysis of Hatch Covers Symbols

$R _ { e H \_ P }$ Yield stress of the plate panel, as defined in 3-2-A8/4.2.1(c).

$R _ { e H \_ S }$ Yield stress of the stiffener, as defined in 3-2-A8/4.2.1(c).

α Aspect ratio of the plate panel, as defined in the Symbol list of 3-2-A8/5.

Allowable buckling utilization factor, as defined in 3-2-A8/1.3.3(a).

## 4.1 General

## 4.1.1 Introduction

4.1.1(a)

The requirements of this Section apply to the buckling assessment of hatch cover structural members based on direct strength analysis (usually by finite element method) and subjected to normal stress, shear stress and lateral pressure.

4.1.1(b)

All structural elements in the direct strength analysis carried out according to Relevant Sections are to be assessed individually. The buckling checks are to be performed for the following structural elements:

● Stiffened and unstiffened panels.

● Web plate in way of openings.

## 4.2 Stiffened and Unstiffened Panels

## 4.2.1 General

4.2.1(a)

The plate panel of a hatch cover structure is to be modelled as stiffened panel (SP) or unstiffened panel (UP), with either Method A or Method B as defined in 3-2-A8/1.3.1(a) to be used for the calculation ofthe plate buckling capacity, which in combination is also equivalent to use the buckling assessment models defined in 3-2-A8/1.3.1(b).

4.2.1(b) Average thickness ofplate panel

For FE analysis, where the plate thickness along a plate panel is not constant, the panel used for the buckling assessment is to be modelled with a weighted average thickness taken as:

$$
t _ {a v r} = \frac {\sum_ {1} ^ {n} A _ {i} t _ {i}}{\sum_ {1} ^ {n} A _ {i}}
$$

where:

$A _ { i }$ = Area of the i-th plate element.

$t _ { i }$ = Net thickness of the i-th plate element.

= Number of finite elements defining the buckling plate panel.

## 4.2.1(c) Yield stress ofthe plate panel and stiffener

The panel yield stress $R _ { e H \_ P }$ is taken as the minimum value of the specified yield stresses of the elements within the plate panel.

The stiffener yield stress $R _ { e H \_ S }$ is taken as the minimum value of the specified yield stresses of the elements within the stiffener.

## 4.2.2 Stiffened Panels

## 4.2.2(a)

For a stiffened panel (SP), each stiffener with attached plate is to be idealized as a stiffened panel model of the extent defined in Relevant Sections.

## 4.2.2(b)

Ifthe stiffener properties or stiffener spacing varies within the stiffened panel, the calculations are to be performed separately for all configurations ofthe panels, i.e., for each stiffener and plate between the stiffeners. Plate thickness, stiffener properties and stiffener spacing at the considered location are to be assumed for the whole panel.

## 4.2.2(c)

The buckling check ofthe stiffeners ofstiffened panels is only applicable to the stiffeners fitted along the longer side edges of the buckling panel.

## 4.2.3 Unstiffened Panels

## 4.2.3(a) Irregular plate panel

In way of web frames and brackets, the geometry of the panel (i.e. plate bounded by web stiffeners/ face plate) may not have a rectangular shape. In this case, for FE analysis, an equivalent rectangular panel is to be defined according to 3-2-A8/4.2.3(b) for irregular geometry and 3-2-A8/4.2.3(c) fo triangular geometry and to comply with buckling assessment.

## 4.2.3(b) Equivalent EPP ofan unstiffenedpanel with irregular geometry

Unstiffened panels with irregular geometry are to be idealized to equivalent panels for plate buckling assessment according to the following procedure:

a) The four corners closest to a right angle, 90 deg, in the bounding polygon for the plate are identified.

![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/bfec886e619035ee8f5a8e95d4f4270f662461646b82f24b4927f580f616be63.jpg)

The distances along the plate bounding polygon between the corners are calculated, i.e. the sum of all the straight-line segments between the end points.

![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/7ebcd3d650b27a8037b87fdbfd964b0aa5c46ee6b848402c2be336d41bf53ce0.jpg)

The pair of opposite edges with the smallest total length is identified, i.e. minimum of $d _ { 1 } + d _ { 3 }$ and $d _ { 2 } + d _ { 4 }$

![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/703276ed8aeb8df822cde26b6e3a6e99ed92248fb90e776a2e9bd7d28dc08b78.jpg)

A line joins the middle points of the chosen opposite edges (i.e. a mid-point is defined as the point at half the distance from one end). This line defines the longitudinal direction for the capacity model. The length of the line defines the length of the capacity model, , measured from one end point.

e) The length of shorter side, , in mm, is to be taken as:

$$
b = \frac {A}{a}
$$

where:

= Area of the plate, in mm<sup>2</sup>

a Length defined in (d), in mm.

![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/34744dbdc76c78629ee008aecbcb08aac47216c32fce922fe3f1d20487e0e180.jpg)

} \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda } \mathbf { \Lambda \Lambda \Lambda \Lambda \mathbf \Lambda \Lambda \Lambda \mathbf \Lambda \Lambda \Lambda \mathbf \Lambda \Lambda \Lambda \mathbf \Lambda \Lambda \mathbf \Lambda \Lambda \Lambda \Lambda \mathbf \Lambda \Lambda \Lambda \mathbf \Lambda \mathbf \Lambda \Lambda \Lambda \mathbf \Lambda \Lambda$ The stresses from the direct strength analysis are to be transformed into the local coordinate system of the equivalent rectangular panel. These stresses are to be used for the buckling assessment.

4.2.3(c) Modelling of an unstiffened plate panel with triangular geometry

Unstiffened panels with triangular geometry are to be idealized to equivalent panels for plate buckling assessment according to the following procedure:

a) Medians are constructed as shown below.

![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/638bff72e005913fd82107e9da40fbf55bf5cdef8eea481c412bf2090275e8a9.jpg)

The longest median is identified. This median the length of which is $l _ { 1 }$ , in mm, defines the longitudinal direction for the capacity model.

![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/01788243b499bcf3bdc41dd0a880e8b6cfef9df8c3f81eff9655a451bcbd4680.jpg)

The width of the model, $l _ { 2 }$ , in mm, is to be taken as:

$$
l _ {2} = \frac {A}{l _ {1}}
$$

where:

= Area of the plate, in $\mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$

![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/a6e31899d612aeaea3b169684c461ea90ce0a1708abe6b4b1ca983a50fab73c2.jpg)

d) The lengths of shorter side, , and of the longer side, , in mm, of the equivalent rectangular plate panel are to be taken as:

$$
b = \frac {l _ {2}}{C _ {t r i}}
$$

$$
a = l _ {1} C _ {t r i}
$$

where:

$$
C _ {t r i} = 0. 4 \frac {l _ {2}}{l _ {1}} + 0. 6
$$

e) The stresses from the direct strength analysis are to be transformed into the local coordinate system of the equivalent rectangular panel and are to be used for the buckling assessment of the equivalent rectangular panel.

## 4.2.4 Reference Stress

4.2.4(a)

The stress distribution is to be taken from the direct strength analysis according to Relevant Sections and applied to the buckling model.

4.2.4(b)

For FE analysis, the reference stresses are to be calculated using the stress-based reference stresses as defined in 3-2-A8/6.

## 4.2.5 Lateral Pressure

4.2.5(a)

The lateral pressure applied to the direct strength analysis is also to be applied to the buckling assessment.

For FE analysis, where the lateral pressure is not constant over a buckling panel defined by a number of finite plate elements, an average lateral pressure, N/mm<sup>2</sup>, is calculated using the following formula:

$$
P _ {a v r} = \frac {\sum_ {1} ^ {n} A _ {i} P _ {i}}{\sum_ {1} ^ {n} A _ {i}}
$$

where:

= Area of the i-th plate element, in mm<sup>2</sup>

$P _ { i }$ = Lateral pressure of the i-th plate element, in N/mm<sup>2</sup>.

n = Number of finite elements in the buckling panel.

## 4.2.6 Buckling Criteria

4.2.6(a) UP-A

The compressive buckling strength of UP-A is to satisfy the following criterion:

ηUP $. { \cal A } \le \eta _ { a l l }$

where:

ηUP-A = Plate buckling utilization factor, equal to as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.2 where UP-A model is to be used.

## 4.2.6(b) UP-B

The compressive buckling strength of UP-B is to satisfy the following criterion:

ηUP−B ≤ ηall

where:

ηUP-B = Plate buckling utilization factor, equal to as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.2 where UP-B model is to be used.

## 4.2.6(c) SP-A

The compressive buckling strength of SP-A is to satisfy the following criterion:

ηSP−A ≤ ηall

where:

ηSP-A = Buckling utilization factor of the stiffened panel, taken as the maximum of the buckling utilization factors calculated as below:

The overall stiffened panel buckling utilization factor as defined in 3-2- A8/5.2.1.

The plate buckling utilization factor as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.2 where SP-A model is to be used.

The stiffener buckling utilization factor as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.3 considering separately the properties (thickness, dimensions), the pressures defined in 3-2-A8/4.2.5(b) and the reference stresses of each EPP at both sides of the stiffener.

Note: The stiffener buckling strength check can only be fulfilled when the overall stiffened panel capacity check, as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.1, is satisfied.

4.2.6(d) SP-B

The compressive buckling strength of SP-B is to satisfy the following criterion:

ηSP−B ≤ ηall

where:

ηSP-B = Buckling utilization factor of the stiffened panel, taken as the maximum of the buckling utilization factors calculated as below:

The overall stiffened panel buckling utilization factor as defined in 3-2- A8/5.2.1.

The plate buckling utilization factor as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.2 where SP-B model is to be used.

The stiffener buckling utilization factor as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.3 considering separately the properties (thickness, dimensions), the pressures defined in 3-2-A8/4.2.5(b) and the reference stresses of each EPP at both sides of the stiffener.

Note: The stiffener buckling strength check can only be fulfilled when the overall stiffened panel capacity check, as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.1, is satisfied.

4.2.6(e) Web plate in way ofopenings

The web plate of primary supporting members with openings is to satisfy the following criterion:

ηopening ≤ ηall

where:

Nopening = Maximum web plate utilization factor in way of openings, calculated with the definition in 3-2-A8/1.3.2(b) and the stress multiplier factor at failure $\gamma _ { c }$ which can be calculated following the requirements in 3-2-A8/5.2.4.

## General

## 5.1.1 Introduction

## 5.1.1(a)

This section contains the methods for determination of the buckling capacities of plate panels, stiffeners, primary supporting members and columns.

## 5.1.1(b)

For the application of this section, the stresses $\sigma _ { x } , \sigma _ { y }$ and applied on the structural members are defined in:

3-2-A8/3 for hull girder prescriptive buckling requirements.

● 3-2-A8/4 for direct strength analysis buckling requirements of hatch covers.

## 5.1.1(c) Buckling capacity

The buckling capacity is calculated by applying the actual stress combination and then increasing or decreasing the stresses proportionally until the interaction formulae defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.1(a), 3-2-A8/5.2.2(a) and 3-2-A8/5.2.3(d) are equal to 1.0, respectively.

## 5.1.1(d) Buckling utilization factor

The buckling utilization factor of the structural member is equal to the highest utilization factor obtained for the different buckling modes.

## 5.1.1(e) Lateral pressure

The lateral pressure is to be applied and considered as constant for the calculation of buckling capacities as defined in 3-2-A8/5.1.1(c).

## 5.2 Buckling Capacity of Plate Panels

## 5.2.1 Overall Stiffened Panels

## 5.2.1(a)

The elastic stiffened panel limit state is based on the following interaction formula, which sets a precondition for the buckling check of stiffeners in accordance with 3-2-A8/5.2.3(d):

$$
\frac {\gamma}{\gamma_ {G E B}} = 1
$$

with the corresponding buckling utilization factor defined as

$$
\eta_ {o v e r a l l} = \frac {1}{\gamma_ {c}}
$$

where the stress multiplier factors of global elastic buckling capacity, , are to be calculated based on the following formulae:

$$
\gamma_ {G E B} = \gamma_ {G E B, b i + \tau} \quad \text {for} \quad \tau \neq 0 \text {and} (\sigma_ {x} > 0 \text {or} \sigma_ {y} > 0)
$$

$$
\gamma_ {G E B} = \gamma_ {G E B, b i} \qquad \mathrm{for} \quad \tau = 0 \mathrm{and} (\sigma_ {x} > 0 \mathrm{or} \sigma_ {y} > 0)
$$

$$
\gamma_ {G E B} = \gamma_ {G E B, \tau} \qquad \mathrm{for} \quad \tau \neq 0 \mathrm{and} (\sigma_ {x} \leq 0 \mathrm{and} \sigma_ {y} \leq 0)
$$

where , and are stress multiplier factors of the global elastic buckling capacity for different load combinations as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.1(b), 3-2-A8/5.2.1(c) and 3-2-A8/5.2.1(d), respectively. For the calculation of , and , neither $\sigma _ { x }$ nor $\sigma _ { y }$ shall be taken less than 0.

$\sigma _ { x } , \sigma _ { y }$ Applied normal stress to the plate panel, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$ , to be taken as defined in 3-2- A8/5.2.2(g).

T Applied shear stress, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$ , to be taken as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.2(g).

## 5.2.1(b)

The stress multiplier factor for the stiffened panel subjected to biaxial loads is taken as:

$$
\gamma_ {G E B, b i} = \frac {\pi^ {2}}{L _ {B 1} ^ {2} L _ {B 2} ^ {2}} \frac {\left[ D _ {1 1} L _ {B 2} ^ {4} + 2 (D _ {1 2} + D _ {3 3}) n ^ {2} L _ {B 1} ^ {2} L _ {B 2} ^ {2} + n ^ {4} D _ {2 2} L _ {B 1} ^ {4} \right]}{L _ {B 2} ^ {2} N _ {x} + n ^ {2} L _ {B 1} ^ {2} N _ {y}}
$$

where:

$N _ { x }$ = Load per unit length applied on the edge along x-axis of the stiffened panel, in N/ mm, taken as:

$$
N _ {x} = \sigma_ {x, a v} (A _ {p} + A _ {s}) / s
$$

For stiffened panels fitted with U-type stiffeners, stiffener spacing is taken as: $s = b _ { 1 } + b _ { 2 }$

where $b _ { 1 }$ and $b _ { 2 }$ are as defined in 3-2-A8/Figure 4.

$N _ { y }$ = Load per unit length applied on the edge along y axis of the stiffened panel, in N/ mm, taken as $N _ { y } = c \sigma _ { y } t _ { p }$

$L _ { B 1 }$ = Stiffener span, in mm, equal to spacing between primary supporting members, i.e. $L _ { B 1 } = \ell$ . Specially, for vertically stiffened side shell of single side skin bulk carriers, $L _ { B 1 } = 0 . 8 \ell$

$L _ { B 2 }$ = Total width of stiffened panel between lateral supports, in mm, taken as 6 times of the stiffener spacing, i.e. 6s.

n = Number of half waves along the direction perpendicular to the stiffener axis. The factor is to be minimized with respect to the wave parameter , i.e. to be taken as the smallest value larger than zero.

C = Factor taking into account the normal stress distribution in the attached plating acting perpendicular to the stiffener’s axis:

$$
c = 0. 5 (1 + \psi) \quad \text { for } \quad 0 \leq \psi \leq 1
$$

$$
c = \frac {1}{2 (1 - \psi)} \qquad \mathrm{for} \quad \psi <   0
$$

$\psi$ = Edge stress ratio for case 2 according to 3-2-A8/Table 5.

= Average stress for both plate and stiffener, taken as:

$$
\begin{array}{l l} \sigma_ {x, a v} = \sigma_ {x} - v c \sigma_ {y} A _ {s} / (A _ {p} + A _ {s}) \geq 0 & \text { for } \quad \sigma_ {x} > 0 \text { and } \sigma_ {y} > 0 \\ \sigma_ {x, a v} = \sigma_ {x} & \text { for } \quad \sigma_ {x} \leq 0 \text { or } \sigma_ {y} \leq 0 \end{array}
$$

$D _ { 1 1 } , D _ { 1 2 } , D _ { 2 2 } , D _ { 3 3 } =$ Bending stiffness coefficients, in Nmm, of the stiffened panel, defined in general as:

$$
D _ {1 1} = \frac {E I _ {e f f} 1 0 ^ {4}}{s}
$$

$$
D _ {1 2} = \frac {E t _ {p} ^ {3} v}{1 2 (1 - v ^ {2})}
$$

$$
D _ {2 2} = \frac {E t _ {p} ^ {3}}{1 2 (1 - v ^ {2})}
$$

$$
D _ {3 3} = \frac {E t _ {p} ^ {3}}{1 2 (1 + v)}
$$

For stiffened panels fitted with U-type stiffeners, $D _ { 1 2 }$ and $D _ { 2 2 }$ are defined as:

$$
D _ {2 2} = \frac {E t _ {p} ^ {3}}{1 2 (1 - v ^ {2})} \left[ 1. 2 + 4. 8 \times M i n \left(1. 0, \frac {b _ {1} ^ {2}}{h _ {w} (b _ {1} + b _ {2})}\right) \times M i n \left(1. 0, \left(\frac {t _ {w}}{t _ {p}}\right) ^ {3}\right) \right]
$$

$$
D _ {1 2} = v D _ {2 2}
$$

$h _ { w }$ is the breadth of U-type stiffener web as defined in 3-2-A8/Figure 4

$I _ { e f f }$ Moment of inertia, in $\mathrm { c m } ^ { 4 } ;$ , of the stiffener including effective width of attached plating, the same as I defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.3(d).

## 5.2.1(c)

The stress multiplier factor for the stiffened panel subjected to pure shear load is taken as:

$$
\gamma_ {G E B, \tau} = \frac {\sqrt [ 4 ]{D _ {1 1} ^ {3} D _ {2 2}}}{(L _ {B} / 2) ^ {2} N _ {x y}} \left[ 8. 1 2 5 + 5. 6 4 \sqrt {\frac {(D _ {1 2} + D _ {3 3}) ^ {2}}{D _ {1 1} D _ {2 2}}} - 0. 6 \frac {(D _ {1 2} + D _ {3 3}) ^ {2}}{D _ {1 1} D _ {2 2}} \right] \quad \mathrm{for} \quad D _ {1 1} D _ {2 2} \geq (D _ {1 2} + D _ {3 3}) ^ {2}
$$

$$
\gamma_ {G E B, \tau} = \frac {\sqrt {2 D _ {1 1} (D _ {1 2} + D _ {3 3})}}{(L _ {B Y} / 2) ^ {2} N _ {x y}} \left[ 8. 3 + 1. 5 2 5 \frac {D _ {1 1} D _ {2 2}}{(D _ {1 2} + D _ {3 3}) ^ {2}} - 0. 4 9 3 \frac {D _ {1 1} ^ {2} D _ {2 2} ^ {2}}{(D _ {1 2} + D _ {3 3}) ^ {4}} \right] \quad \mathrm{for} \quad D _ {1 1} D _ {2 2} <   (D _ {1 2} + D _ {3 3}) ^ {2}
$$

where:

$$
N _ {x y} = \tau t _ {p}
$$

$$
5. 2. 1 (d)
$$

The stress multiplier factor for the stiffened panel subjected to combined loads is taken as:

$$
\gamma_ {G E B, b i + \tau} = \frac {1}{2} \gamma_ {G E B, \tau} ^ {2} \left[ - \frac {1}{\gamma_ {G E B , b i}} + \sqrt {\frac {1}{\gamma_ {G E B , b i} ^ {2}} + 4 \frac {1}{\gamma_ {G E B , \tau} ^ {2}}} \right]
$$

where and are as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.1(b) and 3-2-A8/5.2.1(c), respectively.

## 5.2.2 Plates

5.2.2(a) Plate limit state

The plate limit state is based on the following interaction formulae:

$$
\left(\frac {\gamma_ {c 1} \sigma_ {x} S}{\sigma_ {c x}}\right) ^ {e _ {o}} - B \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c 1} \sigma_ {x} S}{\sigma_ {c x}}\right) ^ {\frac {e _ {o}}{2}} \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c 1} \sigma_ {y} S}{\sigma_ {c y}}\right) ^ {\frac {e _ {o}}{2}} + \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c 1} \sigma_ {y} S}{\sigma_ {c y}}\right) ^ {e _ {o}} + \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c 1} | \tau | S}{\tau_ {c}}\right) ^ {e _ {o}} = 1
$$

$$
\left(\frac {\gamma_ {c 2} \sigma_ {x} S}{\sigma_ {c x}}\right) ^ {\frac {2}{\beta_ {p} ^ {0 . 2 5}}} + \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c 2} | \tau | S}{\tau_ {c}}\right) ^ {\frac {2}{\beta_ {p} ^ {0 . 2 5}}} = 1 f o r \sigma_ {x} \geq 0
$$

$$
\left(\frac {\gamma_ {c 3} \sigma_ {y} S}{\sigma_ {c y}}\right) ^ {\frac {2}{\beta_ {p} ^ {0 . 2 5}}} + \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c 3} | \tau | S}{\tau_ {c}}\right) ^ {\frac {2}{\beta_ {p} ^ {0 . 2 5}}} = 1 f o r \sigma_ {y} \geq 0
$$

$$
\frac {\gamma_ {c 4} | \tau | S}{\tau_ {c}} = 1
$$

with

$$
\gamma_ {c} = m i n \left(\gamma_ {c 1}, \gamma_ {c 2}, \gamma_ {c 3}, \gamma_ {c 4}\right)
$$

and the corresponding buckling utilization factor defined as

$$
\eta_ {p l a t e} = \frac {1}{\gamma_ {c}}
$$

where:

$\sigma _ { x } , \sigma _ { y }$ = Applied normal stress to the plate panel, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$ , to be taken as defined in $3 { - } 2 { - } \mathrm { A } 8 / 5 . 2 . 2 ( \mathrm { g } )$

$\tau$ = Applied shear stress to the plate panel, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$

$\sigma _ { c x }$ = Ultimate buckling stress, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 } ;$ , in direction parallel to the longer edge of the buckling panel as defined in $3 – 2 – \mathrm { A } 8 / 5 . 2 . 2 ( \mathrm { c } )$

$\sigma _ { c y }$ = Ultimate buckling stress, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 } ,$ in direction parallel to the shorter edge of the buckling panel as defined in $3 – 2 – \mathrm { A } 8 / 5 . 2 . 2 ( \mathrm { c } )$

$\tau _ { c }$ = Ultimate buckling shear stresses, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$ , as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.2(c).

= Stress multiplier factors at failure for each of the above different limit states. and $\gamma _ { c 3 }$ are only to be considered when $\sigma _ { x } \ge 0$ and $\sigma _ { y } \geq 0$ respectively.

$B$ = Coefficient given in $3 { - } 2 { - } \mathrm { A } 8 / \mathrm { T a b l e } \ 3$

$e _ { 0 }$ = Coefficient given in 3-2-A8/Table 3.

$\beta _ { p }$ = Plate slenderness parameter taken as:

$$
\beta_ {p} = \frac {b}{t _ {p}} \sqrt {\frac {R _ {e H \_ P}}{E}}
$$

## 5.2.2(b) Reference degree of slenderness

The reference degree of slenderness is to be taken as:

$$
\lambda = \sqrt {\frac {R _ {e H \_ P}}{K \sigma_ {E}}}
$$

where:

= Buckling factor, as defined in 3-2-A8/Table 5 and 3-2-A8/Table 6.

## 5.2.2(c) Ultimate buckling stresses

The ultimate buckling stresses of plate panels, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 } ;$ , are to be taken as:

$$
\sigma_ {c x} = C _ {x} R _ {e H \_ P}
$$

$$
\sigma_ {c y} = C _ {y} R _ {e H \_ P}
$$

The ultimate buckling stress of plate panels subject to shear, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$ , is to be taken as:

$$
\tau_ {c} = C _ {\tau} \frac {R _ {e H \_ P}}{\sqrt {3}}
$$

where:

, , = Reduction factors, as defined in 3-2-A8/Table 5.

For the 1<sup>st</sup> Equation of 3-2-A8/5.2.2(a), when $\sigma _ { x } \ < 0$ or $\sigma _ { y } < 0$ , the reduction factors are to taken as:

$$
C _ {x} = C _ {y} = C _ {\tau} = 1.
$$

● For the other cases:

For SP-A and UP-A, $C _ { y }$ is calculated according to 3-2-A8/Table 5 by using

$$
c _ {1} = \left(1 - \frac {1}{\alpha}\right) \geq 0
$$

For SP-B and UP-B, $C _ { y }$ is calculated according to 3-2-A8/Table 5 by using $c _ { 1 } = 1$

For vertically stiffened single side skin of bulk carrier, $C _ { y }$ is calculated according to 3-2- A8/Table 5 by using

$$
c _ {1} = \left(1 - \frac {1}{\alpha}\right) \geq 0
$$

For corrugation of corrugated bulkheads, $C _ { y }$ is calculated according to 3-2-A8/Table 5 by using

$$
c _ {1} = \left(1 - \frac {1}{\alpha}\right) \geq 0
$$

The boundary conditions for plates are to be considered as simply supported, see cases 1, 2 and 15 of 3-2-A8/Table 5. If the boundary conditions differ significantly from simple support, a more appropriate boundary condition can be applied according to the different cases of Table 5 subject to the agreement of ABS.

## 5.2.2(d) Correctionfactor $F _ { l o n g }$

The correction factor $F _ { l o n g }$ depending on the edge stiffener types on the longer side of the buckling panel is defined in 3-2-A8/Table 4. An average value of $F _ { l o n g }$ is to be used for plate panels having different edge stiffeners. For stiffener types other than those mentioned in 3-2-A8/Table 4, the value of is to be agreed by ABS. In such a case, value of higher than those mentioned in 3-2-A8/ Table 4 can be used, provided it is verified by buckling strength check of panel using non-linear FE analysis and deemed appropriate by ABS.

The correction factor $F _ { t r a n }$ is to be taken as:

For transversely framed EPP of single side skin bulk carrier, between the hopper and top wing tank:

– $F _ { t r a n } = 1 . 2 5$ when the two adjacent frames are supported by one tripping bracket fitted in way of the adjacent plate panels.

$F _ { t r a n } ~ = 1 . 3 3$ when the two adjacent frames are supported by two tripping brackets each fitted in way of the adjacent plate panels.

$F _ { t r a n } = 1 . 1 5$ elsewhere.

● For the attached plate of a U-type stiffener fitted on a hatch cover:

$$
F _ {t r a n} = \operatorname{Max} \left(3 - 0. 0 8 \left(F _ {t r a n 0} - 6\right) ^ {2}, 1. 0\right) \leq 2. 2 5
$$

where:

$$

$$

$$

with $b _ { 1 } , \ b _ { 2 }$ and $h _ { w }$ as defined in 3-2-A8/Figure 4.

Coefficient defined in Case 2 of 3-2-A8/Table 5 is to be replaced by the following formula:

$$

## 5.2.2(f) Curved plate panels

This requirement for curved plate limit state is applicable when $R / t _ { p } \ \leq \ 2 5 0 0$ . Otherwise, the requirement for plate limit state given in 3-2-A8/5.2.2(a) is applicable.

The curved plate limit state is based on the following interaction formula:

$$
\left(\frac {\gamma_ {c} \sigma_ {a x} S}{C _ {a x} R _ {e H \_ P}}\right) ^ {1. 2 5} - 0. 5 \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c} \sigma_ {a x} S}{C _ {a x} R _ {e H \_ P}}\right) \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c} \sigma_ {t g} S}{C _ {t g} R _ {e H \_ P}}\right) + \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c} \sigma_ {t g} S}{C _ {t g} R _ {e H \_ P}}\right) ^ {1. 2 5} + \left(\frac {\gamma_ {c} \tau \sqrt {3} S}{C _ {\tau} R _ {e H \_ P}}\right) ^ {2} = 1. 0
$$

with the corresponding buckling utilization factor defined as

$$
\eta_ {c u r v e d \_ p l a t e} = \frac {1}{\gamma_ {c}}
$$

where:

$\sigma _ { a x }$ 二 Applied axial stress to the cylinder corresponding to the curved plate panel, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$ . In case of tensile axial stresses, $\sigma _ { a x } = 0$

$\sigma _ { t g }$ = Applied tangential stress to the cylinder corresponding to the curved plate panel, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$ . In case of tensile tangential stresses, $\sigma _ { t g } = 0$

$C _ { a x } , C _ { t g } , C _ { \tau }$ = Buckling reduction factor of the curved plate panel, as defined in 3-2-A8/ Table 6.

The stress multiplier factor, $\gamma _ { c }$ , of the curved plate panel need not be taken less than the stress multiplier factor, for the expanded plane panel according to 5A-8-5/2.2.1.

5.2.2(g) Applied normal and shear stresses to plate panels

The normal stress, $\sigma _ { x }$ and $\sigma _ { y } .$ , in N/mm<sup>2</sup>, to be applied for the overall stiffened panel capacity and the plate panel capacity calculations as given in 3-2-A8/5.2.1(a) and 3-2-A8/5.2.2(a) respectively, are to be taken as follows:

For FE analysis, the reference stresses as defined in 3-2-A8/4.2.4.

For prescriptive assessment of the overall stiffened panel capacity and the plate panel capacity, the axial or transverse compressive stresses calculated according to Relevant Sections, at load calculation points ofthe considered stiffener or the considered elementary plate panel, as defined in item a) and item b) of 3-2-A8/3.1.2(a) respectively. However, in case of transverse stiffening arrangement, the transverse compressive stress used for the assessment of the overall stiffened panel capacity is to be taken as the compressive stress calculated at load calculation points of the stiffener attached plating, as defined in item a) of 3-2-A8/3.1.2(a).

● For grillage analysis where the stresses are obtained based on beam theory, the stresses taken as:

$$
\sigma_ {x} = \frac {\sigma_ {x b} + v \sigma_ {y b}}{1 - v ^ {2}}
$$

$$
\sigma_ {y} = \frac {\sigma_ {y b} + v \sigma_ {x b}}{1 - v ^ {2}}
$$

Where

= Stress, in N/mm<sup>2</sup>, from grillage beam analysis respectively along x or y axis of the plate attached to the PSM web.

The shear stress , in N/mm<sup>2</sup>, to be applied for the overall stiffened panel capacity and the plate panel capacity calculations as given in 3-2-A8/5.2.1(a) and 3-2-A8/5.2.2(a) respectively, are to be taken as follows:

● For FE analysis, the reference shear stresses as defined in 3-2-A8/4.2.4.

For prescriptive assessment of the plate panel capacity, the shear stresses calculated according to Relevant Sections, at load calculation points of the considered elementary plate panel, as defined in item a) of 3-2-A8/3.1.2(a).

For prescriptive assessment of the overall stiffened panel capacity, the shear stresses calculated according to Relevant Sections, at the following load calculation point:

At the middle of the full span, , of the considered stiffener.

At the intersection point between the stiffener and its attached plating.

For grillage beam analysis, $\tau = 0$ in the plate attached to the PSM web.

## 5.2.3 Stiffeners

5.2.3(a) Buckling modes

The following buckling modes are to be checked:

Stiffener induced failure (SI).

Associated plate induced failure (PI).

5.2.3(b) Web thickness of flat bar

For accounting the decrease of the stiffness due to local lateral deformation, the effective web thickness of flat bar stiffener, in mm, is to be used in 3-2-A8/5.2.1 and 3-2-A8/5.2.3(d) for the calculation of the net sectional area, $A _ { s }$ , the net section modulus, , and the moment of inertia, , of the stiffener and is taken as:

$$
t _ {w \_ r e d} = t _ {w} \left(1 - \frac {2 \pi^ {2}}{3} \left(\frac {h _ {w}}{S}\right) ^ {2} \left(1 - \frac {b _ {e f f 1}}{S}\right)\right)
$$

## 5.2.3(c) Idealization ofbulb profile

Bulb profiles are to be considered as equivalent angle profiles. The net dimensions of the equivalent built-up section are to be obtained, in mm, from the following formulae.

$$
h _ {w} = \dot {h _ {w}} - \frac {\dot {h _ {w}}}{9 . 2} + 2
$$

$$
b _ {f} = \alpha \left(t _ {w} ^ {\prime} + \frac {h _ {w} ^ {\prime}}{6 . 7} - 2\right)
$$

$$
t _ {f} = \frac {h _ {w} ^ {\prime}}{9 . 2} - 2
$$

$$
t _ {w} = \dot {t _ {w}}
$$

where:

$h _ { w } ^ { ' } , t _ { w } ^ { ' }$ = Net height and thickness of a bulb section, in mm, as shown in 3-2-A8/Figure 11.

Coefficient equal to $\begin{array} { l l } { { \displaystyle \alpha = 1 . 1 + \frac { \big ( 1 2 0 - h _ { w } ^ { ' } \big ) ^ { 2 } } { 3 0 0 0 } } } & { { \mathrm { f o r } h _ { w } ^ { ' } \leq 1 2 0 } } \\ { { \displaystyle \alpha = 1 . 0 } } & { { \mathrm { f o r } h _ { w } ^ { ' } > 1 2 0 } } \end{array}$ α =

5.2.3(d) Ultimate buckling capacity

When $\sigma _ { a } + \sigma _ { b } + \sigma _ { w } > 0$ while initially setting $\gamma = 1$ , the ultimate buckling capacity for stiffeners is to be checked according to the following interaction formula:

$$
\frac {\gamma_ {c} \sigma_ {a} + \sigma_ {b} + \sigma_ {w}}{R _ {e H}} S = 1
$$

with the corresponding buckling utilization factor defined as

$$
\eta_ {s t i f f e n e r} = \frac {1}{\gamma_ {c}}
$$

where:

$\sigma _ { a }$ = Effective axial stress, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 } ;$ , at mid span of the stiffener, acting on the stiffener with its attached plating.

$$
\sigma_ {a} = \sigma_ {x} \frac {s t _ {p} + A _ {s}}{b _ {e f f 1} t _ {p} + A _ {s}}
$$

$\sigma _ { x }$ = Nominal axial stress, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 } ,$ acting on the stiffener with its attached plating.

For FE analysis, $\sigma _ { x }$ is the FE corrected stress as defined in $3 – 2 – \mathrm { A } 8 / 5 . 2 . 3 ( \mathrm { f } )$ in the attached plating in the direction of the stiffener axis.

For prescriptive assessment, $\sigma _ { x }$ is the axial stress calculated according to $3 { - } 2 { - } \hat { \bf A } 8 / 3 . 2 \hat { . } 2 ( { \bf a } )$ at load calculation point of the stiffener, as defined in 3-2- A8/3.1.2(a).

For grillage beam analysis, $\sigma _ { x }$ is the stress acting along the x-axis of the attached buckling panel.

$R _ { e H }$ = Specified minimum yield stress of the material, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$

$R _ { e H } = R _ { e H } \_ S$ for stiffener induced failure $( S I ) .$

$R e H = R _ { e H - p }$ for plate induced failure $( P I ) .$

$\sigma _ { b }$ = Bending stress in the stiffener, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$

$$
\sigma_ {b} = \frac {M _ {o} + M _ {1} + M _ {2}}{1 0 0 0 Z}
$$

$Z$ = Net section modulus of stiffener, in $\mathrm { c m } ^ { 3 } ,$ , including effective width of plating according to 3-2-A8/5.2.3(e), to be taken as:

The section modulus calculated at the top ofstiffener flange for stiffener induced failure (SI).

● The section modulus calculated at the attached plating for plate induced failure $( P I )$

$M _ { 2 }$ = Bending moment, in Nmm, due to eccentricity of sniped stiffeners, to be taken as: $M _ { 2 } = 0$ for continuous stiffeners

$M _ { 2 } = C _ { s n i p } W _ { n a } \gamma \sigma _ { x } \left( A _ { p } + A _ { s } \right)$ for stiffeners sniped at one or both ends.

$C _ { s n i p }$ = Coefficient to account for the end effect of the stiffener sniped at one or both ends, to be taken as:

$C _ { s n i p } = - 1 . 2$ for stiffener induced failure (SI)

$C _ { s n i p } = 1 . 2$ for plate induced failure $( P I )$

$M _ { 1 }$ = Bending moment, in Nmm, due to the lateral load $P \colon$

$M _ { 1 } = C _ { i } \frac { \left| P \right| s l ^ { 2 } } { 2 4 \times 1 0 ^ { 3 } }$ for continuous stiffener

$M _ { 1 } = C _ { i } \frac { \left| P \right| s l ^ { 2 } } { 8 \times 1 0 ^ { 3 } }$ for sniped stiffener

$M _ { 1 } = C _ { i } \frac { \left| P \right| s l ^ { 2 } } { 1 4 . 2 \times 1 0 ^ { 3 } }$ for stiffener sniped at one end and continuous at the other end

$P$ Lateral load, in $\mathrm { k N } / \mathrm { m } ^ { 2 } .$

For FE analysis, $P$ is the average pressure as defined in 3-2-A8/4.2.5(b) in the attached plating.

For prescriptive assessment, $P$ is the pressure calculated at load calculation point of the stiffener, as defined in 3-2-A8/3.1.2(a).

$C _ { i }$ = Pressure coefficient:

$C _ { i } = C _ { S I }$ for stiffener induced failure $( S I )$

$C _ { i } = C _ { P I }$ for plate induced failure $( P I ) .$

$C _ { P I }$ = Plate induced failure pressure coefficient:

$C _ { P I } = 1$ if the lateral pressure is applied on the side opposite to the stiffener. $C _ { P I } = - 1$ if the lateral pressure is applied on the same side as the stiffener.

$C _ { S I }$ = Stiffener induced failure pressure coefficient:

$C _ { S I } = - 1$ if the lateral pressure is applied on the side opposite to the stiffener. $C _ { S I } = 1$ if the lateral pressure is applied on the same side as the stiffener.

$M _ { o }$ = Bending moment, in Nmm, due to the lateral deformation w of stiffener:

$M _ { o } = F _ { E } C _ { s l } \frac { \gamma } { \gamma _ { G E B } - \gamma }$ w0with preconditior $\gamma _ { G E B } - \gamma > 0$

Stress multiplier factor of global elastic buckling capacity as defined in 3-2- γGEB = A8/5.2.1.

$F _ { E }$ Ideal elastic buckling force of the stiffener, in ${ \bf N } .$

$$
F _ {E} = \left(\frac {\pi}{l}\right) ^ {2} E I \cdot 1 0 ^ {4}
$$

$I$ = Moment of inertia, in $\mathrm { c m } ^ { 4 } ,$ of the stiffener including effective width of attached plating according to $3 – 2 – A 8 / 5 . 2 . 3 ( \mathrm { e } )$ . is to comply with the following requirement:

$$
I \geq \frac {s t _ {p} ^ {3}}{1 2 \cdot 1 0 ^ {4}}
$$

$$
t _ {p}
$$

= Net thickness of plate, in mm, to be taken as

● For prescriptive requirements: the mean thickness of the two attached plating panels,

● For FE analysis: the thickness of the considered EPP on one side of the stiffener.

$C _ { s l }$ = Deformation reduction factor to account for global slenderness, to be taken as:

$$
C _ {s l} = 1 - \frac {1}{1 2} \lambda_ {G} ^ {4} \qquad \mathrm{for} \qquad \lambda_ {G} \leq 1. 5 6
$$

$$
C _ {s l} = \frac {3}{\lambda_ {G} ^ {4}} \qquad \mathrm{for} \qquad \lambda_ {G} > 1. 5 6
$$

$\lambda _ { G }$ = Reference degree of global slenderness of the stiffened panel, to be taken as:

$$
\lambda_ {G} = \sqrt {\frac {\gamma_ {R e H}}{\gamma_ {G E B}}} \mathrm{with} \gamma_ {R e h} = \frac {m i n (R _ {e H \_ P} , R _ {e H \_ s})}{\sqrt {\sigma_ {x , a v} ^ {2} + \sigma_ {y} ^ {2} - \sigma_ {x , a v} \sigma_ {y} + 3 \tau_ {x y} ^ {2}}}
$$

$\sigma _ { x , a v }$ = Average stress for both plate and stiffener as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.1(b).

$\sigma _ { y }$ = Applied transverse stress to the plate panel as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.1(a).

$\tau$ = Applied shear stress to the plate panel as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.1(a).

$w _ { 0 }$ = Assumed imperfection, in mm, to be taken as:

$$
w _ {0} = l / 1 0 0 0
$$

$\sigma _ { w }$ = Stress due to torsional deformation, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 } ,$ , to be taken as:

● For stiffener induced failure (SI)

## 5.2.4(a) Web plate in way of openings

The web plate of primary supporting members with openings is to be assessed for buckling based on the combined axial compressive and shear stresses.

The web plate adjacent to the opening on both sides is to be considered as individual unstiffened plate panels as shown in 3-2-A8/Table 8.

The interaction formulae of 3-2-A8/5.2.2(a) are to be used with:

$$
\sigma_ {x} = \sigma_ {a v}
$$

$$
\sigma_ {y} = 0
$$

$$
\tau = \tau_ {a v}
$$

where:

σav = Weighted average compressive stress, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 } ,$ , in the area of web plate being considered, i.e. P1, P2 or P3 as shown in 3-2-A8/Table 8.

For the application of the Table 8, the weighted average shear stress is to be taken as:

● Opening modelled in primary supporting members:

$\tau _ { a v }$ = Weighted average shear stress, in N/mm<sup>2</sup>, in the area of web plate being considered, i.e. P1, P2, or P3 as shown in 3-2-A8/Table 8.

● Opening not modelled in primary supporting members:

$\tau _ { a v }$ = Weighted average shear stress, in N/mm<sup>2</sup>, given in 3-2-A8/Table 8.

## 5.2.4(b) Reduction factors of web plate in way of openings

The reduction factors, $C _ { x }$ or $C _ { y }$ in combination with, of the plate panel(s) of the web adjacent to the opening is to be taken as shown in 3-2-A8/Table 8.

5.2.4(c)

The equivalent plate panel of web plate of primary supporting members crossed by perpendicular stiffeners is to be idealized as shown in 3-2-A8/Figure 12.

## 5.2.5 Stiffened Panels with U-type Stiffeners

## 5.2.5(a) Local plate buckling

For stiffened panels with U-type stiffeners, local plate buckling is to be checked for each of the plate panels EPP $b _ { 1 } , \ b _ { 2 } , \ b _ { f }$ and $h _ { w }$ (see 3-2-A8/Figure 4) separately as follows:

The attached plate panels EPP $b _ { 1 }$ and $b _ { 2 }$ are to be assessed using SP-A model, where in the calculation of buckling factors $K _ { x }$ as defined in Case 1 of Table 5, the correction factor $F _ { l o n g }$ for U-type stiffeners as defined in 3-2-A8/Table 4 is to be used; and in the calculation of $K _ { y }$ as defined in Case 2 of3-2-A8/Table 5, the $F _ { t r a n }$ for U-type stiffeners as defined in 3-2-A8/5.2.2.5] is to be used.

● The face plate and web plate panels $b _ { f }$ and $h _ { w }$ are to be assessed using UP-B model with $F _ { l o n g } = 1$ and $F _ { t r a n } = 1$

## 5.2.5(b) Overall stiffened panel buckling and stiffener buckling

For a stiffened panel with U-type stiffeners, the overall buckling capacity and ultimate capacity of the stiffeners are to be checked with warping stress $\sigma _ { w } = 0$ , and with bending moment of inertia including effective width of attached plating being calculated based on the following assumptions:

The two web panels of a U-type stiffener are to be taken as perpendicular to the attached plate with thickness equal to $t _ { w }$ and height equal to the distance between the attached plate and the face plate of the stiffener.

Effective width of the attached plating, $b _ { e f f }$ , taken as the sum of the $b _ { e f f }$ calculated for the EPP $b _ { 1 }$ and $b _ { 2 }$ respectively according to SP-A model.

Effective width of the attached plating of a stiffener without shear lag effect, $b _ { e f f 1 }$ , taken as the sum of the $b _ { e f f 1 }$ calculated for the EPP $b _ { 1 }$ and respectively.

## 5.3 Buckling Capacity of Column Structures

## 5.3.1 Column Buckling of Corrugations

## 5.3.1(a) Buckling utilization factor

The column buckling utilization factor, , for axially compressed corrugations is to be taken as:

$$
\eta_ {c o l u m n} = \frac {\sigma_ {a v}}{\sigma_ {c r}}
$$

where:

$\sigma _ { a v }$ = Average axial compressive stress in the member, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$

= Minimum critical buckling stress, in N/mm<sup>2</sup>, taken as:

$\sigma _ { c r } = \sigma _ { E } \mathrm { f o r } \sigma _ { E } \leq 0 . 5 R _ { e H \_ S }$

$$
\sigma_ {c r} = \left(1 - \frac {R _ {e H \_ S}}{4 \sigma_ {E}}\right) R _ {e H \_ S} \text { for } \sigma_ {E} > 0. 5 R _ {e H \_ S}
$$

$\sigma _ { E }$ = Elastic column compressive buckling stress, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$ , according to 3-2- A8/5.3.1(b).

$R _ { e H \_ S }$ = Specified minimum yield stress of the considered member, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 } .$ . For built-up members, the lowest specified minimum yield stress is to be used.

## 5.3.1(b) Elastic column buckling stress

The elastic compressive column buckling stress, in $\mathrm { N } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 2 }$ of members subject to axial compression is to be taken as:

$$
\sigma_ {E} = \pi^ {2} E f _ {e n d} \frac {I}{A l _ {p i l l} ^ {2}} 1 0 ^ {- 4}
$$

where:

= Net moment of inertia about the weakest axis of the cross section, in cm<sup>4</sup>.

= Net cross sectional area of the member, in cm<sup>2</sup>.

$l _ { p i l l }$ = Unsupported length of the member, in m.

$f _ { e n d }$ = End constraint factor, corresponding to simply supported ends is to be applied except for fixed end support to be used in way of stool with width exceeding 2 times the depth of the corrugation, taken as:

$f _ { e n d } = 1 . 0$ where both ends are simply supported.

● $f _ { e n d } = 2 . 0$ where one end is simply supported and the other end is fixed.

$f _ { e n d } = 4 . 0$ where both ends are fixed.

## 6.1 Stress Based Method

## 6.1.1 Introduction

6.1.1(a)

This section provides a method to determine stress distribution along edges of the considered buckling panel by second-order polynomial curve, by linear distribution using least square method and by weighted average approach. This method is called Stress based Method. The reference stress is the stress components at centre of plate element transferred into the local system of the considered buckling panel.

## 6.1.1(b) Definition

A regular panel is a plate panel of rectangular shape. An irregular panel is plate panel which is not regular, as detailed in 3-2-A8/4.2.3(a).

## 6.1.2 Stress Application

## 6.1.2(a) Regular panel

The reference stresses are to be taken as defined in 3-2-A8/6.2.1 for a regular panel when the following conditions are satisfied:

At least, one plate element centre is located in each third part of the long edge of a regular panel and

● This element centre is located at a distance in the panel local direction not less than $a / 4$ to at least one of the element centres in the adjacent third part of the panel.

Otherwise, the reference stresses are to be taken as defined in 3-2-A8/6.2.2 for an irregular panel.

6.1.2(b) Irregular panel and curvedpanel

The reference stresses of an irregular panel or of a curved panel are to be taken as defined in 3-2- A8/6.2.2.

## 6.2 Reference Stresses

## 6.2.1 Regular Panel

6.2.1(a) Longitudinal stress

The longitudinal stress $\sigma _ { x }$ applied on the shorter edge of the buckling panel is to be calculated as follows:

For plate buckling assessment, the distribution of $\sigma _ { x } \left( x \right)$ is assumed as second order polynomial curve as:

$$
\sigma_ {x} (x) = C \cdot x ^ {2} + D x + E
$$

The best fitting curve $\sigma _ { x } \left( x \right)$ is to be obtained by minimizing the square error $\prod$ considering the area of each element as a weighting factor.

$$
\prod = \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \left[ \sigma_ {i x} - (C x _ {i} ^ {2} + D x _ {i} + E) \right] ^ {2}
$$

The unknown coefficients $C , D$ and E must yield zero first derivatives, $\partial \Pi$ with respect to $C ,$ D and E respectively.

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \frac {\partial \prod}{\partial C} = 2 \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i} ^ {2} \left[ \sigma_ {x i} - (C x _ {i} ^ {2} + D x _ {i} + E) \right] = 0 \end{array} \right.
$$

$$
\frac {\partial \prod}{\partial D} = 2 \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i} \left[ \sigma_ {x i} - (C x _ {i} ^ {2} + D x _ {i} + E) \right] = 0
$$

$$
\frac {\partial \prod}{\partial E} = 2 \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \left[ \sigma_ {x i} - \left(C x _ {i} ^ {2} + D x _ {i} + E\right) \right] = 0
$$

The unknown coefficients $C , D$ and E can be obtained by solving the 3 above equations.

$$
\sigma_ {x 1} = \frac {1}{b} \int_ {0} ^ {b} \sigma_ {x} (x) d x = \frac {b ^ {2}}{3} C + \frac {b}{2} D + E
$$

$$
\sigma_ {x 2} = \frac {1}{b} \int_ {a - b} ^ {a} \sigma_ {x} (x) d x = \left(a ^ {2} - a b + \frac {b ^ {2}}{3}\right) C + \left(a - \frac {b}{2}\right) D + E
$$

$\mathrm { I f } - \frac { D } { 2 C } < \frac { b } { 2 } \ \mathrm { o r } \ - \frac { D } { 2 C } > a - \frac { b } { 2 } , \sigma _ { x 3 }$ is to be ignored. Otherwise, $\sigma _ { x 3 }$ is taken as:

$$
\sigma_ {x 3} = \frac {1}{b} \int_ {x _ {\min}} ^ {x _ {\max}} \sigma_ {x} (x) d x = \frac {b ^ {2}}{1 2} C - \frac {D ^ {2}}{4 C} + E
$$

where:

$$
x _ {m i n} = - \frac {b}{2} - \frac {D}{2 C} x _ {m a x} = \frac {b}{2} - \frac {D}{2 C}
$$

The longitudinal stress is to be taken as:

$$
\sigma_ {x} = M a x (\sigma_ {x 1}, \sigma_ {x 2}, \sigma_ {x 3})
$$

The edge stress ratio is to be taken as:

$$
\psi_ {x} = 1
$$

For overall stiffened panel buckling and stiffener buckling assessments, $\sigma _ { x } \left( x \right)$ applied on the shorter edge of the attached plate is to be taken as:

$$
\sigma_ {x} = \frac {\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \sigma_ {x i}}{\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i}}
$$

The edge stress ratio $\psi _ { x }$ for the stress $\sigma _ { x }$ is equal to 1.0.

## 6.2.1(b) Transverse stress

The transverse stress $\sigma _ { y }$ applied along the longer edges of the buckling panel is to be calculated by extrapolation of the transverse stresses of all elements up to the shorter edges of the considered buckling panel.

FIGURE 13 Buckling Panel  
![](ABS-Rules_for_Building_and_Classing_Marine_Vessels%E2%80%94Part3-Hull_Construction_and_Equipment/part-0401-0600/images/6a7bc59482e41444b789674092e65915accefb658d6e901485c59601d9e4d025.jpg)

The distribution of $\sigma _ { y } \left( x \right)$ is assumed as straight line. Therefore: $\sigma _ { y } ( x ) = A + B x$

The best fitting curve $\sigma _ { y } \left( x \right)$ is to be obtained by the least square method minimizing the square error considering area of each element as a weighting factor.

$$
\Pi = \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \left[ \sigma_ {y i} - (A + B x _ {i}) \right] ^ {2}
$$

The unknown coefficients $C$ and $D$ must yield zero first partial derivatives, with respect to $C$ and $D ,$ respectively.

$$
\frac {\partial \Pi}{\partial A} = 2 \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} [ \sigma_ {y i} - (A + B x _ {i}) ] = 0
$$

$$
\frac {\partial \Pi}{\partial B} = 2 \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i} [ \sigma_ {y i} - (A + B x _ {i}) ] = 0
$$

The unknown coefficients A and B are obtained by solving the 2 above equations and are given as follow:

$$
A = \frac {\left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \sigma_ {y i}\right) \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i} ^ {2}\right) - \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i}\right) \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i} \sigma_ {y i}\right)}{\left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i}\right) \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i} ^ {2}\right) - \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i}\right) ^ {2}}
$$

$$
B = \frac {\left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i}\right) \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i} \sigma_ {y i}\right) - \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i}\right) \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \sigma_ {y i}\right)}{\left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i}\right) \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i} ^ {2}\right) - \left(\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} x _ {i}\right) ^ {2}}
$$

The transverse stress is to be taken as:

$$
\sigma_ {y} = \max (A, A + B a)
$$

The edge stress ratio is to be taken as:

$$
\psi_ {y} = \frac {\min (A , A + B a}{\max (A , A + B a)} \mathrm{for} \sigma_ {y} \geq 0
$$

$$
\psi_ {y} = 1 \mathrm{for} \sigma_ {y} <   0
$$

## 6.2.1(c) Shear stress

The shear stress is to be calculated using a weighted average approach, and is to be taken as:

$$
\tau = \frac {\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \tau_ {i}}{\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i}}
$$

## 6.2.2 Irregular Panel and Curved Panel

## 6.2.2(a) Reference stresses

The longitudinal, transverse and shear stresses are to be calculated using a weighted average approach. They are to be taken as:

$$
\sigma_ {x} = \frac {\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \sigma_ {x i}}{\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i}}
$$

$$
\sigma_ {y} = \frac {\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \sigma_ {y i}}{\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i}}
$$

$$
\tau = \frac {\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i} \tau_ {i}}{\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} A _ {i}}
$$

The edge stress ratios are to be taken as:

$$
\psi_ {x} = 1
$$

$$
\psi_ {y} = 1
$$

PART 3

C H A P T E R 3

Subdivision and Stability

S E C T I O N 1

General Requirements

## 1 General (2024)

Part 3, Chapter 3, Section 1 (referred to as Section 3-3-1) covers provisions for general requirements of subdivision and stability.

## 1.1 Objective

## 1.1.1 Goals

The vessel is to be designed, constructed, operated, and maintained to:

<table><tr><td>Goal No.</td><td>Goals</td></tr><tr><td>STAB 1</td><td>have adequate watertight integrity and restoring energy to prevent capsize in an intact condition.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB 2</td><td>have adequate subvision and stability to provide survivability to damage or accidental conditions.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB 6</td><td>provide means to control the overall vessel weight and distribution to maintain adequate trim and stability.</td></tr><tr><td>MGMT 3</td><td>establish procedures, plans and instructions for operations concerning the safety of the personnel, vessel, and protection of the environment (ISM Code 7)</td></tr><tr><td>MGMT 4</td><td>establish procedures, plans and instructions for emergency situations concerning the safety of the personnel, vessel, and protection of the environment. (ISM Code 7)</td></tr><tr><td>PROP 6</td><td>be provided with means to enable the safe conduct of all towing, mooring, and anchoring operations. (SOLAS II-1 Reg 3-8.2)</td></tr></table>

## 1.1.2 Functional Requirements

To achieve the above-stated goals, the design, construction, and maintenance of subdivision and stability is to be in accordance with the following functional requirements, as applicable:

<table><tr><td>Functional Requirement No.</td><td>Functional Requirements</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Stability (STAB)</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR1</td><td>Provide adequate watertight integrity and restoring energy (intact stability) to prevent capsize in all loading conditions and foreseeable operating conditions including severe weather, icing, dead ship, rolling resonance, and water trapped on deck.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR2 (PROP)</td><td>Have sufficient intact stability to carry out anchor handling/towing operations.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR3</td><td>Have sufficient intact stability to carry out lifting operations.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR4</td><td>Have sufficient intact stability to account for the effect of free surfaces of liquids in tanks.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR5</td><td>Remain afloat and stable when damage to the hull causes subsequent loss of watertight integrity.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR6</td><td>Provide the means to control the overall weight and distribution to maintain adequate trim and stability.</td></tr><tr><td>STAB-FR7</td><td>Accurately calculate lightship characteristics and monitor changes to buoyancy and weight throughout the vessel&#x27;s operating life.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Safety Management (MGMT)</td></tr><tr><td>MGMT-FR1 (STAB)</td><td>Provide information to enable the master by rapid and simple processes to obtain accurate guidance as to the stability and applicable intact and damage stability requirements of the ship under varying conditions of service.</td></tr></table>

## 1.1.3 Compliance

A vessel is considered to comply with the goals and functional requirements within the scope of classification when the applicable prescriptive requirements are complied with or when an alternative arrangement has been approved. Refer to Part 1D, Chapter 2.

## 2 Application Scope (2025)

i) Vessels of characteristics within the scope of [TABLE 1] are to meet the stability and subdivision criteria specified in the following sections, as applicable.

ii) In case the criteria listed in this Section are not applicable to a particular vessel, the intact and damage stability are to be reviewed by ABS in accordance with other recognized criteria appropriate to the vessel’s type, size and intended service.

iii) Vessels that are configured as mobile offshore units are to comply with the subdivision and stability requirements of the ABS Rules for Building and Classing Offshore Units (Offshore Rules).

iv) In the situation where the stability review is conducted and found satisfactory by the flag State Administration, the stability information and calculations specified in the following sections need not be submitted.

v) Attained subdivision index “A” calculated by ABS in accordance with Regulation II-1/7 of SOLAS 1974 as amended is to be indicated in the Record.

## 3 Review Procedures (1 July 2020)

## 3.1 Submission of Plans (2024)

The following subdivision and stability drawings and documents, as applicable, are to be submitted for ABS review:

i) Trim and Stability Booklet or simplified guidance for Master

ii) General arrangement plan, with outboard profil

iii) Capacity plan or table with centers of gravity and free surface values for tanks and holds

Lines plan

v) Tank Sounding Tables, if not included in the Trim and Stability Booklet.

vi) Cross curves of stability, if not included in the Trim and Stability Booklet.

vii) List of down-flooding points, including their transverse, longitudinal and vertical locations, used in the calculation of the intact and damage stability criteria.

viii) Draft Marks. Drawing showing the draft mark details, longitudinal locations of marks fore and aft referenced to the forward and after perpendiculars or to the nearest frames and vertical reference points. Navigational draft marks should be based on the vessel's lowest vertical projection.

ix) Intact and damage (if required) stability calculations supporting the max. KG or min. GM curve

x) Stability Test Procedure

xi) Stability Test Results

xii) Hydrostatic table, if not included in the Trim and Stability Booklet

xiii) Damage control plan and damage control booklet for vessels where damage stability is required

## 3.3 Administration Review

## 3.3.1

Where the vessel is issued a certificate by the flag Administration or its agent other than ABS, such Certificate may be accepted as evidence that the vessel has subdivision and stability in accordance with the criteria in the respective Convention. Examples of these certificates are listed below:

SOLAS Cargo Ship Safety Construction Certificate

International Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Liquefied Gases in Bulk

International Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk

● International Load Line Certificate

● International Oil Pollution Prevention Certificate

● Passenger Ship Safety Certificate

Cargo Ship Safety Construction Certificate

## 3.3.2

Where the Administration undertakes the review of subdivision and stability and ABS is issuing one or more of the above Certificates, the acceptance of subdivision and stability by the Administration is required before the certificate is issued.

## 3.5 ABS Review

In all other cases, the information and calculations for subdivision and stability are to be submitted to ABS for review.

## 5 Criteria

## 5.1 Intact Stability (2024)

Vessels of applicable size, type and service are to comply with the intact stability criteria as indicated in 3-3-1/Table 1.

The requirements of this section are appliable to new construction vessels based on the keel lay date.

For vessels undergoing modifications, the stability criteria applicable at time of construction or major modification may be applied. The latest stability criteria are applicable if the hydrostatic properties or internal subdivision have been modified.

Vessels under 24 m (79 ft) in length are to meet intact stability requirements of a recognized standard.

Vessels of applicable size, type and service are to comply with the subdivision and damage stability criteria as indicated in 3-3-1/Table 2:
